items.head: Four catches in loss
items.body: Allen caught four of eight targets for 26 yards during Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Allen led the team in targets, but he was only able to compile 26 yards, his lowest output since Week 2. The wide receiver hasn't reached the end zone in his last five games, and the Colts' offense as a whole has struggled mightily recently. On the year, Allen has reeled in 40 of 58 targets for 351 yards and one score over eight contests, and his next chance to reach paydirt will come in Week 10 versus the Dolphins.

items.head: Seahawks to start QB Drew Lock vs. Raiders, giving Sam Darnold more time to heal
items.body: The Seahawks plan to start quarterback Drew Lock on Sunday against the Raiders, giving Sam Darnold more time to recover from his injuries.

items.head: Encouraging results regarding oblique injury
items.body: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Lock's tests on his oblique injury were "good," and the issue is something the QB is expected to manage ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders,  Gregg Bell of The Tacoma News Tribune reports. As a result, it seems likely that Lock's practice reps will be managed this week in order to prepare him for another starting assignment, with fellow signal caller Sam Darnold -- who was inactive in Week 9 -- not ready to return to the lineup this weekend. The Seahawks have a bye in Week 11, which may afford Darnold enough time to return to action Nov. 29 against the 49ers, but barring any setbacks it looks like Lock is bound to fill in again, backed up by Jalen Milroe.

items.head: Drew Lock (Oblique) is Questionable
items.body: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Lock's tests on his oblique injury were "good," and the issue is something the QB is expected to manage ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders,  Gregg Bell of The Tacoma News Tribune reports.

items.head: Injures oblique during Week 9 win
items.body: Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said after Sunday's 17-3 win over the Cardinals that Lock sustained an oblique injury during the game, leaving Lock's availability for Week 10 against the Raiders up in the air, Bob Condotta of the Seattle Times reports. Lock finished the win over Arizona, completing 19 of 28 passes for 175 yards and a touchdown while adding five rushing attempts for 16 yards. His lone touchdown pass was a seven-yard connection to AJ Barner with 15 seconds left in the first half. Sam Darnold (quadriceps) sat out Sunday's win and may not be ready to return against the Raiders. If both Lock and Darnold sit out, 2025 third-round pick Jalen Milroe would make his first regular-season start.

items.head: Set for Week 9 start
items.body: Lock (right elbow) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Lock logged three consecutive limited sessions this week due to the right elbow injury that has relegated him to inactive status as the emergency third quarterback the last two games. However, with his status now cleared up for Week 9 action, he's set to fill in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) for at least one contest. In two previous appearances (one start) in place of Darnold in Weeks 1 and 2, Lock completed 35 of 48 passes (73 percent) for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions and had two carries for 13 yards. Jalen Milroe will back up Lock on Sunday.

items.head: Another limited practice
items.body: Lock (right elbow) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Lock is poised to fill in for Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) this Sunday against the Cardinals, but the former still has some work to do to avoid a designation for that contest after a second straight capped session to begin Week 9 prep. Friday's injury report will reveal if Lock's right elbow issue is behind him, though he appears close to being healthy, as he told Brady Henderson of ESPN.com on Thursday that it's "doing a lot better... (It) felt great to get under center, rip some balls yesterday."

items.head: Listed as limited Wednesday
items.body: Lock (right elbow) was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. The Seahawks ruled out Sam Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, which places Lock in line for his second start of the campaign. However, Lock suffered a right elbow injury during Week 7 prep that left him as Seattle's emergency third quarterback the last two games. Assuming he gains clearance to suit up in Week 9, he'll be under center for Sunday's NFC West matchup.

items.head: Set to start Sunday
items.body: Lock (elbow) is slated to start Sunday's game against the Cardinals, per NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano. Siciliano adds that Lock has an elbow injury that the team will manage during the week, but he's nonetheless set to get the starting assignment Sunday with fellow signal caller Sam Darnold unavailable due to quad and rib issues. Beyond this weekend, it's possible that Lock's QB1 stint could continue given that Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports that Darnold is viewed as week-to-week, according to coach Mike Macdonald.

items.head: No action in Week 9
items.body: Giddens did not appear in Sunday's 27-23 loss to the Cowboys. Giddens didn't see any action after turning six carries into 43 yards in Week 8 against the Jaguars. With Jonathan Taylor potentially set to be traded before Tuesday's NFL trade deadline, Giddens would stand to operate as the team's No. 2 option in the backfield behind rookie Seth McGowan upon Taylor's departure.

items.head: Demond Claiborne (Knee) is Injured Reserve
items.body: ir

items.head: Two snags in victory
items.body: Spann-Ford caught two of three targets for 20 yards during Sunday's 27-23 win versus the Colts. Spann-Ford opened Week 9 in his typical reserve role behind Jake Ferguson at tight end, but Ferguson suffered a knee injury in the third quarter. With Ferguson set to miss multiple weeks of action, Spann-Ford will have a chance to operate as the team's primary option at tight end beginning in Week 10 versus the 49ers. On the year, Spann-Ford has reeled in 19 of 27 targets for 136 yards and four touchdowns over nine regular-season contests so far.

items.head: Schottenheimer: Cowboys will be without Ferguson, Goodson for 'multiple weeks'
items.body: The Dallas Cowboys will be without starting tight end Jake Ferguson and No. 2 running back Tyler Goodson for "multiple weeks," coach Brian Schottenheimer told reporters Monday, a day after his team posted a 27-23 victory against the Indianapolis Colts.

items.head: Set for multi-week absence
items.body: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said Monday that Goodson will miss "multiple weeks" after spraining his knee in Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports. Goodson will likely undergo further testing as the Cowboys look to hone in on a more definitive timeline for his return, but Schottenheimer's comments suggest that the reserve running back can safely be ruled out for at least Week 10 against the 49ers and Week 11 versus the Titans. Despite succumbing to the knee injury, the 25-year-old delivered his best performance of the season Sunday, finishing the day with 77 yards on 12 carries. The Cowboys currently have no other healthy running backs on the roster beyond starter Javonte Williams, but one or both of practice-squad members Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin will be candidates for elevation to the 53-man roster while Goodson is sidelin

items.head: Likely out for Week 10
items.body: Cowboys executive vice president Stephen Jones said Monday that Goodson is expected to miss time after injuring his knee in Sunday's 27-23 win over the Colts, Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram reports. Goodson has emerged as the Cowboys' clear No. 2 back in recent games and turned in his best performance of the season against his former Colts squad in Week 9, carrying 12 times for 77 yards while failing to corral his lone target. The running back injured his knee at some point along the way, and though he was able to check back into the contest, Goodson may have been running on adrenaline. He'll presumably undergo further testing before the Cowboys provide an update on the extent of his injury, but with Goodman on track to miss at least next Sunday's game versus the 49ers, Dallas could turn to practice-squad members Israel Abanikanda and Jashaun Corbin to serve in backup roles behind lead

items.head: Strong showing against former squad
items.body: Goodson rushed 12 times for 77 yards and failed to bring in his only target in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. Facing the team for which he played two-plus seasons from 2023-25, Goodson put together a highly efficient performance as a complementary option to Javonte Williams, even after leaving the game for a spell to be checked out for a knee issue. Goodson's carry and yardage totals were both season highs, as was his average of 6.4 yards per carry. The Iowa product is seeing steady usage in a run-heavy Cowboys offense, and he's logged 29 rush attempts over the last three games heading into a Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers.

items.head: Returns to game
items.body: Goodson (knee) has returned to Sunday's game against the Colts, Mike Chappell of Fox 59 News Indianapolis reports. Goodson returned in the third quarter of Sunday's contest after previously exiting with a knee injury. Now that he's back in action, Goodson should continue to work in his usual change-of-pace role behind Javonte Williams for the remainder of the game.

items.head: Exits with knee injury
items.body: Goodson (knee) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports. Goodson exited in the second quarter of Sunday's contest with a knee issue after compiling 44 yards on seven carries. Javonte Williams is the sole remaining active running back active for the Cowboys in Week 9.

items.head: Dealing with hip issue
items.body: Okonkwo was deemed a limited participant on Washington's estimated practice report Monday due to a hip injury, John Keim of ESPN.com reports. Okonkwo appears to have gotten hurt in Sunday's loss to the Rams, though he logged his usual offensive snap share (74 percent) and finished with s solid 6-57-0 receiving line on seven targets. The Commanders didn't actually practice Monday, so the tight end's level of activity -- if any -- Tuesday should provide more clarity about whether he's at risk of missing Thursday's clash against the Giants. Washington has been hurt by injuries to its wideout corps, and Okonkwo has stepped up with 57 or more receiving yards in three of the team's past four games.

items.head: Chig Okonkwo (Hip) is Questionable
items.body: Okonkwo was deemed a limited participant on Washington's estimated practice report Monday due to a hip injury, John Keim of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Six snags in loss
items.body: Okonkwo caught six of seven targets for 57 yards during Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. Okonkwo finished tied for the team lead in targets with wide receiver Van Jefferson, reeling in at least five passes for the second time in three games. The tight end's seven targets matched a season high, and he is still searching for his first touchdown as a member of the Commanders after joining the team in the offseason.

items.head: Headed to Arizona
items.body: Johnson was signed by the Cardinals off Cincinnati's practice squad Monday, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Johnson will head to Arizona to join his 15th NFL team in 14 NFL seasons. The quarterback is likely poised to operate as the team's primary backup option behind rookie Carson Beck as Beck replaces Gardner Minshew (elbow) as the team's starting QB in Week 10 against the Rams. Minshew is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 campaign while recovering from a torn UCL, so Johnson will likely stick around Arizona until the season's conclusion.

items.head: Considered limited Monday
items.body: Mooney (chest) was estimated to be a limited participant at the Giants' walkthrough practice Monday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports. Mooney reeled in a season-high three passes for 54 yards and also had a rush for minus-4 yards during Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. The wide receiver may have picked up a chest injury during the victory, and as a result, he was considered to be less than 100 percent Monday. Mooney will have two more chances to be upgraded to a full participant prior to Thursday night's matchup with the Commanders.

items.head: Darnell Mooney (Chest) is Questionable
items.body: Mooney (chest) was estimated to be a limited participant at the Giants' walkthrough practice Monday, Dan Salomone of the team's official site reports.

items.head: Set to take over as QB1
items.body: Beck is expected to start Sunday's contest against the Rams, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports. Beck is slated to take over as Arizona's starting quarterback in Week 10, with Gardner Minshew (elbow) potentially set to miss the remainder of the 2026 season with a torn UCL. Beck has yet to appear in a regular-season contest in his rookie campaign, but he completed 15 of 19 passes for 188 yards and a touchdown in his lone preseason appearance. Lead running back Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is still on injured reserve for at least three more contests and top wide receiver Michael Wilson (neck) suffered a season-ending injury in Week 9, so Beck will have to make do with limited options around him in Arizona.

items.head: Estimated as DNP on Monday
items.body: Burks (foot) was deemed a non-participant on the Commanders' practice report Monday, John Keim of ESPN.com reports. Washington didn't actually practice Monday, so Burks' participation -- or lack thereof -- Tuesday should be more useful in providing insight into the wideout's chance of suiting up Thursday against the Giants. Burks didn't play this past Sunday in a loss to the Rams after sitting out practice all of last week. Terry McLaurin (knee) is out for the season, and Dyami Brown (calf) landed on IR on Saturday, so Burks will likely have a prominent role in the Commanders' passing game Thursday if he's able to suit up.

items.head: Could be back for Week 10
items.body: Commanders head coach Dan Quinn said Monday that he's "more optimistic" that Burks (foot) will be available for Thursday's game against the Giants, John Keim of ESPN.com reports. Quinn expects to have better feel for Burks' status Tuesday, when the team will hold the most intense of its light practices leading up to Thursday's game. Burks was unable to play in this past Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams due to the foot injury, but once healthy, he'll likely be in line for a regular top-three role at receiver while Terry McLaurin (knee) is lost for the season.

items.head: Ruled out for Week 9
items.body: Burks (foot) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Rams. With Burks out and Dyami Brown (calf) injured in Friday's practice, the Commanders could be digging even deeper into their depth at wide receiver after Terry McLaurin suffered a season-ending knee injury two weeks ago. Look for Stefon Diggs and Antonio Williams to be every-down wideouts against Los Angeles.

items.head: No practice Thursday
items.body: Burks (foot) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice. Burks is mimicking his practice regimen from a week ago, when he kicked it off with back-to-back DNPs due to a foot issue. If he follows last week's regimen, he'll be limited Friday and enter the weekend listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Rams. While playing through the injury this past Sunday against the Eagles, he tallied a 68 percent snap share and recorded three catches (on five targets) for 81 yards.

items.head: DNP on Wednesday
items.body: Burks (foot) did not practice Wednesday, Ben Standig of The Team 980 Washington D.C. reports. After back-to-back DNPs last Wednesday and Thursday, Burks got in a limited session Friday before being cleared to play Sunday night against Philly. He ended up recording three grabs for 81 yards as the Commanders' leading receiver in the contest. Burks should play plenty of snaps the rest of the season with Terry McLaurin (knee) done for the year.

items.head: Status for Week 10 remains uncertain
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) has a chance to play Sunday against San Francisco, but his practice reps will likely again be capped this week, Jon Machota of The Athletic reports. Pickens was limited in practice all of last week and ultimately didn't suit up Sunday against Indianapolis. There had been some optimism that he'd be able to participate in that contest, so there's a decent chance that he'll be able to return to action versus the 49ers. Nonetheless, Pickens could again be given a designation heading into this weekend if he doesn't manage at least one full practice before the Cowboys' final injury report is released Friday.

items.head: Inactive in Week 9
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) is inactive for Sunday's game at Indianapolis. For a second week in a row, Pickens endured practice restrictions due to a hamstring injury, leaving him questionable to suit up in Week 9. On Friday, head coach Brian Schottenheimer told Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site that he was "hopeful" Pickens would be available this weekend, but that didn't come to pass. With Pickens and fellow WR KaVontae Turpin (ribs) inactive Sunday, CeeDee Lamb, Ryan Flournoy, Jonathan Mingo, Camden Brown and Jordan Hudson will compose Dallas' receiving corps.

items.head: Questionable for Week 9
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game at Indianapolis, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports. Pickens' practice reps were capped all week due to a lingering hamstring injury. Head coach Brian Schottenheimer told Yarrish on Friday that he's "hopeful" Pickens will be able to suit up this weekend, and Dallas will confirm as much about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

items.head: Will remain limited Friday
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) "will be a little bit limited" Friday, but head coach Brian Schottenheimer is "hopeful" he will play Sunday against the Colts, Tommy Yarrish of the Cowboys' official site reports. Pickens was limited at practice both Wednesday and Thursday due to a hamstring issue, and it appears he will find himself in a similar spot at Friday's practice. The Cowboys will provide another update on his status after the latest session comes to a close.

items.head: Another limited session
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) was limited at Thursday's practice, Todd Archer of ESPN.com reports. Pickens maintained his activity level from Wednesday as he deals with lingering shoulder and hamstring injuries. He still was able to handle a 57 percent snap share this past Sunday against the Cardinals, but he mustered only two catches (on four targets) for 48 yards. Friday's practice report will unveil whether or not Pickens heads into the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Indianapolis.

items.head: Limited in Wednesday's practice
items.body: Pickens (hamstring) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports. Pickens was limited by shoulder and hamstring injuries last week, but he was able to suit up this past Sunday against the Cardinals, logging a 57 percent snap share and gathering in two of four targets for 48 yards. As Week 9 prep kicks off, he's being listed with only the hamstring issue, which continues to impact his on-field work. Pickens will have two more chances to get back to full Thursday and Friday before Dallas potentially tags him with a designation for Sunday's contest at Indianapolis.

items.head: Expected back after Week 11 bye
items.body: Darnold (quadriceps), who won't play this coming Sunday at Las Vegas, is expected to return in Week 12 at San Francisco on Sunday, Nov. 29 after a Week 11 bye, Gregg Bell of Sports Radio 93.3 KJR Seattle reports. Darnold is one week removed from suffering a quad injury and cracked ribs in a Week 8 loss to the Bears, which sidelined him Sunday against the Cardinals and will keep him in street clothes in Week 10. For as long as Darnold is sidelined, Drew Lock (oblique) is lined up to be the Seahawks' starting quarterback.

items.head: Not ready to return in Week 10
items.body: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Monday that Darnold (quadriceps/ribs) won't be available for Sunday's game against the Raiders, John Boyle of the team's official site reports. Meanwhile, Macdonald noted that the Seahawks got a "good exam" for Drew Lock, who is nursing an oblique injury but is expected to be able to play through the issue and make a second straight start in Week 10. With a bye on tap for the Seahawks in Week 11, Darnold will benefit from some extended time to recover from his injuries and will turn his focus toward returning to action Nov. 29 versus the 49ers.

items.head: Could miss Week 10
items.body: Darnold (quadriceps) may miss Seattle's Week 10 game at Las Vegas, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Darnold already has been ruled out for Sunday's contest against the Cardinals, and the combination of the quadriceps injury and cracked ribs he suffered last Monday against the Bears is threatening to sideline him for multiple weeks. The Seahawks have a Week 11 bye on the schedule, so getting him healthy for the stretch run from late November through early January may sway the team's decision-making. As long as Darnold is out, Drew Lock (right elbow) will direct Seattle's offense.

items.head: Won't play in Week 9
items.body: Head coach Mike Macdonald announced that Darnold won't play Sunday against the Cardinals due to a quadriceps injury, NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano reports. In addition to a quad issue that Darnold sustained late in Monday's loss to the Bears, Macdonald revealed that the quarterback suffered a rib injury early in that contest. The pair of health concerns may have played a part in Darnold's subpar performance, which included 188 yards, two touchdowns and one interception on 17-for-34 passing and two carries for 20 yards. With Darnold out for the first time since Week 2, backup QB Drew Lock will draw the Week 9 start under center for the Seahawks.

items.head: Middling numbers in Week 8 loss
items.body: Darnold completed 17 of 34 passes for 188 yards with two touchdowns and one interception while adding two rushes for 20 yards in the Seahawks' 34-17 loss to the Bears on Monday night. Darnold averaged just 5.5 yards per attempt and took three sacks from a Bears defense that made an impact addition in Jeffery Simmons on Thursday via trade with the Titans. Darnold's 50.0 percent completion rate was a season low for him in non-injury-shortened games, and the veteran signal-caller also threw an interception for the sixth consecutive contest. Darnold did toss multiple touchdowns for the first time since Week 4, connecting with Jaxon Smith-Njigba (43 yards) and Cooper Kupp (seven yards) for his pair of scoring strikes. Darnold will take an unsightly 10:9 TD:INT heading into a Week 9 home matchup against the Cardinals on Sunday.

items.head: Tyrell Shavers (Knee - ACL) is Out
items.body: Shavers (knee) was not activated from the reserve/PUP list ahead of Monday night's matchup with Minnesota, per the NFL's official transaction log.

items.head: Charlie Jones (Thumb) is Questionable
items.body: questionable

items.head: Managing hip issue
items.body: McCarthy (hip) is listed as limited on Monday's practice estimate, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. McCarthy exited Sunday's win at Philadelphia for a spell in the third quarter due to a hip injury but returned to action. Head coach John Harbaugh told Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News on Monday that McCarthy has a hip pointer but is expected to play Thursday versus the Commanders. McCarthy likely will need to be listed as full Tuesday and/or Wednesday to head into Week 10 action without a designation.

items.head: J.J. McCarthy (Hip) is Questionable
items.body: McCarthy (hip) is listed as limited on Monday's practice estimate, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports.

items.head: Harbaugh: Giants 'feel fairly good' about McCarthy (hip) playing vs. Commanders
items.body: Giants coach John Harbaugh says he feels "fairly good" about quarterback J.J. McCarthy's availability this week after he suffered a hip injury in Sunday's win against the Eagles.

items.head: Likely to play Thursday, despite hip pointer
items.body: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Monday that McCarthy is managing a hip pointer but is expected to play Thursday against the Commanders, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports. "It does look like he's gonna play," Harbaugh said. "I feel fairly good about it." During Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles, McCarthy exited with just over 12 minutes left in the third quarter due to the hip issue and appeared to be in significant discomfort while attempting to test out the injury by throwing on the sideline. Backup Jameis Winston stepped in to finish out the Giants' possession and directed another drive before McCarthy was able to check back into the contest for the final play of the quarter. Though he finished out the game for the Giants, McCarthy still looks to be less than 100 percent, and his practice reps could be affected on a short week. However, barring a major downturn in his condition, McCarthy should be ready to start Thursday's contest.

items.head: Ineffective in Week 9 win
items.body: McCarthy (hip) completed 12 of 19 passes for 127 yards and rushed four times for 22 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. McCarthy left the game in the third quarter due to a hip injury, and Jameis Winston led the Giants' only touchdown drive of the game before McCarthy checked back in on the following possession. Winston's small-sample success Sunday probably won't be enough to wrestle the starting role back from McCarthy, but McCarthy's Week 10 availability could be in question with a short week to recover before the Giants host the Commanders on Thursday. It wasn't pretty, but the 5-2-1 Giants maintained some breathing room in the NFC East, even with the Cowboys improving to 4-5, while the 2-7 Eagles and 2-5-1 Commanders dropped further out of contention.

items.head: Back in Sunday's game
items.body: McCarthy (hip) returned to Sunday's contest at Philadelphia, Connor Hughes of SNY.tv reports. McCarthy exited Week 9 action for a spell in the third quarter due to a hip injury, but it couldn't keep him from coming back on to the field near the end of that period. Barring a setback, he'll look to finish out the game.

items.head: Injures hip in Week 9
items.body: McCarthy suffered a hip injury during Sunday's game in Philadelphia. McCarthy was on the receiving end of a big hit from Eagles linebacker Zack Baun in the third quarter and was in clear pain as he went to the sideline tent, and eventually, the locker room. The nature of the issue is known, but considering McCarthy is questionable to return, he still has a chance to reenter the contest. Jameis Winston has taken over for McCarthy under center.

items.head: Visits sideline tent Sunday
items.body: McCarthy (undisclosed) went to the blue medical tent during Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports. McCarthy took a big hit to the midsection from Eagles linebacker Zack Baun in the third quarter and was in obvious discomfort as he went to the sideline. The nature of McCarthy's injury isn't known, but Jameis Winston will fill in for him for as long as he's out of the contest.

items.head: Deemed day-to-day by Harbaugh
items.body: Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh noted Monday that McConkey is viewed as "day to day" with back spasms, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports. McConkey was not among the Chargers' Week 9 inactives, but he didn't play any snaps in Sunday's loss to the Texans after experiencing back spasms during pregame workouts. Harbaugh's assessment that the wideout is 'day-to-day' offers hope that McConkey will be in the clear ahead of next Monday's game against the Ravens, and a big step toward that outcome would be his full participation in practice no later than Saturday.

items.head: Pregame back spasms lead to Week 9 absence
items.body: McConkey was active but didn't play any snaps in Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Texans after experiencing back spasms during pregame workouts, Noah Furtado of The Athletic reports. Because McConkey sustained the injury after the Chargers had already announced their inactive list, the wideout ended up being active but unavailable for the second time in three games. Back in Week 5, McConkey had been managing a foot injury but still proceeded to suit up for a matchup with Denver, though he didn't see any action and was active only because the Chargers had seven other players dealing with more significant health concerns. McConkey also made early exits in Week 1 due to a rib injury, Week 4 due to the foot issue and in Week 6 due to a concussion. The mounting injuries have made it increasingly difficult for fantasy managers to depend on McConkey, whose lack of availability

items.head: Exits Sunday's game
items.body: McConkey (back) is questionable to return to Sunday's game against the Texans. Prior to his first-quarter exit, McConkey wasn't targeted by QB Justin Herbert. His absence leaves Quentin Johnston, Tre' Harris, KeAndre Lambert-Smith and Derius Davis as the Chargers' available WRs versus Houston.

items.head: Limited at Monday's walkthrough
items.body: Skattebo (hamstring) was listed as limited on Monday's estimated injury report, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Skattebo missed his first game of the season Sunday in Philadelphia due to a hamstring injury that he sustained in the Giants' previous game back in Week 7. Prior to Skattebo being inactive, though, Adam Schefter of ESPN reported that the running back was pushing to play, and head coach John Harbaugh told Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News on Monday that he should be "full go" for Thursday's game against the Commanders. Skattebo still has some work to do to prove his health, but he appears to be trending in the right direction for a Week 10 appearance.

items.head: Looks ready to go for Week 10
items.body: Giants head coach John Harbaugh said Monday that Skattebo (hamstring) should be "full go" for Thursday's game against the Commanders, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports. After tweaking his hamstring in an Oct. 25 overtime win over the Texans, Skattebo wasn't able to fully shake the injury coming out of a Week 8 bye and ended up missing his first game of the season Sunday in the Giants' 19-11 win over the Eagles. The second-year back was at least able to close Week 9 prep as a limited participant in practice, and Harbaugh noted that Skattebo was close to playing against the Eagles before the team ultimately chose to hold him out as a matter of caution. Though the Giants will face a quick turnaround for Week 10, Skattebo looks on track to reclaim a leading role out of the backfield against Washington, barring a setback with his hamstring during the team's limi

items.head: Doubtful for Week 9
items.body: Skattebo (hamstring) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Skattebo was able to manage one limited practice (Friday) this week, and while head coach John Harbaugh told Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post that the Giants are "keeping the door open" for the running back to play in Week 9, his official listing implies it's more likely just ajar. In any case, if Skattebo ends up sitting out Sunday, Devin Singletary likely will serve as New York's lead runner, with Greg Desrosiers and potentially practice-squad members Eric Gray and Phil Mafah in line for work behind him.

items.head: Has chance to play Sunday
items.body: Head coach John Harbaugh said Skattebo (hamstring) didn't practice Friday, but the Giants are "keeping the door open" for the running back to play Sunday at Philadelphia, Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post reports. Skattebo wasn't able to practice this week due to the hamstring injury that he sustained near the end of the Giants' last game in Week 7 at Houston. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported Friday morning that Skattebo was trending toward sitting out in Week 9, but Harbaugh's comments run contrary to that. It appears as if Skattebo will be listed as something other than 'out' once the team posts its final practice report of the week Friday afternoon.

items.head: Not doing much at Friday's practice
items.body: Skattebo (hamstring) was in uniform but not participating at the start of Friday's practice, Jordan Raanan of ESPN reports. It remains to be seen if Skattebo will do enough to get a 'limited' designation. He didn't practice Wednesday or Thursday, and NFL Network's Ian Rapoport already reported that Skattebo is unlikely to play Sunday at Philadelphia. That leaves Devin Singletary as the probable starter and possible three-down workhorse, backed by only undrafted rookie Greg Desrosiers on the active roster (Eric Gray and Phil Mafah are on the practice squad).

items.head: Seemingly out for Week 9
items.body: "It does not seem" that Skattebo (hamstring) will play Sunday against the Eagles, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. A hamstring injury sustained prior to the Giants' Week 8 bye prevented Skattebo from practicing both Wednesday and Thursday, and although he will have one more chance to get some work in before game designations are determined, it appears the injury will keep him off the field for Week 9.

items.head: Remains sidelined at practice
items.body: Skattebo (hamstring) was a non-participant at Thursday's practice, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Coming out of New York's Week 8 bye, Skattebo hasn't been able to practice this week due to the hamstring injury that he suffered near the end of a Week 7 win at Houston. Friday's injury report will reveal his odds to suit up Sunday at Philadelphia, but if Skattebo is inhibited or sidelined, Devin Singletary is the next player up in the Giants backfield, Greg Desrosiers is the only other RB on the active roster, and Eric Gray and Phil Mafah are candidates to be elevated from the practice squad.

items.head: Working with trainers Thursday
items.body: Skattebo (hamstring) was spotted working off to the side with the Giants' training staff Thursday, Art Stapleton of The Bergen Record reports. Per Dan Duggan of The Athletic, Skattebo didn't have his helmet on in doing so. The Giants' upcoming injury report will reveal the running back's official participation level, but if Skattebo is limited or out Sunday against the Eagles, Devin Singletary is next in line for added work, with Greg Desrosiers and possibly practice-squad members Eric Gray and Phil Mafah also in the mix.

items.head: Skyler Bell (Coach's Decision) is Out
items.body: inactive

items.head: Active for MNF
items.body: Beckham is active for Monday's game against the Bills, Ben Goessling of The Minnesota Star Tribune reports. Beckham joined Minnesota's active roster Monday, and he will have a chance to make his first appearance for the team the same evening. It's unclear what role he will step into, but with Jauan Jennings (calf) unavailable, he will be in the mix with Tai Felton and Myles Price behind starters Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.

items.head: Signs with Minnesota's active roster
items.body: The Vikings are signing Beckham from the practice squad to the active roster, Tom Pelissero of NFL Network reports. Beckham kicked off the season with the Giants but was targeted just one time through the first three contests before the team released him Sept. 29. He then joined the Vikings on the practice squad and was elevated for Week 5 but eventually was inactive. Thus, if Beckham is able to avoid such a listing Monday against the Bills, it'll mark the sixth different organization in which he's suited up in his career.

items.head: Brandon Aiyuk reinstated by NFL; 49ers have 2-game roster exemption for receiver
items.body: The NFL reinstated San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk on Monday after he reported for a physical, according to the league's transaction wire.

items.head: Reinstated, 49ers granted two-week exemption
items.body: The 49ers reinstated Aiyuk (personal) from the reserve/left squad list Monday and were granted a two-week roster exemption for the wide receiver, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. In what amounted to a procedural transaction after Aiyuk met with team officials Friday upon filing his paperwork for reinstatement, the 49ers now have until Nov. 23 to either add him to the 53-man roster, release him or trade him. Given that Aiyuk owes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture, securing a release from the team could prove difficult, though it's possible that the two sides work out a repayment plan that would allow him to become a free agent. In addition to the financial complications potentially delaying Aiyuk's return to the field, it's unclear if the 49ers or any other team have interest in rostering the 28-year-old wideout, who hasn't played an NFL snap since tea

items.head: Brandon Aiyuk (Personal) is Out
items.body: The 49ers reinstated Aiyuk (personal) from the reserve/left squad list Monday and were granted a two-week roster exemption for the wide receiver, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports.

items.head: Meets with 49ers on Friday
items.body: Prior to meeting with 49ers officials Friday, Aiyuk (personal) told assembled media that he's "feeling great, healthy" and "looking to get reinstated to the National Football League," Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. Per Wagoner, Aiyuk submitted paperwork to be reinstated to the NFL in late October, and since then both the NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association have been involved in an attempt to reach a resolution that's agreeable to both the wide receiver and the 49ers. Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Thursday that Aiyuk's efforts to secure his release may be hampered by the roughly $13 million in bonus forfeitures that he owes the team, which could mean arbitration comes into play and delays the process. Friday's meeting between Aiyuk, his agent Drew Rosenhaus and San Francisco brass was only the first step. If the sides reach an agreement, the 49ers will have three options: release

items.head: Money owed may be hurdle in securing release
items.body: Aiyuk's effort to secure his release by reporting to the 49ers' facility Friday could be complicated by roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture he owes the team, Tom Pelissero of NFL Network reports. Pelissero notes that the NFL Management Council and the NFL Players Association are both involved in trying to reaching a resolution that is agreeable to both Aiyuk and the 49ers. It's possible that the embattled wideout could ultimately agree to pay back the money in order to potentially have an opportunity to move on with another club, but there's also a chance the issue goes to arbitration. Aiyuk is planning to show up at San Francisco's facility Friday, though that is unlikely to bring the matter to a close. In fact, it could take an extended period of time to sort out a path forward, especially if arbitration is brought into play.

items.head: Path forward murky
items.body: Head coach Kyle Shanahan and GM John Lynch both declined to get into specifics when discussing the future of Aiyuk, who has filed his paperwork for reinstatement and plans to show up to the 49ers' facility Friday, Eric Branch of the San Francisco Chronicle reports. Lynch previously stated "I think it's safe to say that he's played his last snap with the Niners" regarding Aiyuk in January, but the GM was much less definitive Thursday when asked about a reunion with Aiyuk, responding with "I think everything's possible." Head coach Kyle Shanahan gave a similar answer Wednesday, stating "There's no absolutes in life." The 49ers are working with the NFL management council to find a resolution to Aiyuk's situation, so the team's front office and coaching staff are treating this situation as an ongoing legal matter. If Aiyuk is successfully reinstated, the 49ers could trade him, release him or add him to the active roster.

items.head: Turns in reinstatement paperwork
items.body: Aiyuk, who who currently is on the 49ers' Reserve/Left Squad list, has turned in paperwork to be reinstated, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. Per his agent Drew Rosenhaus, Aiyuk "is healthy and ready to get back on the field." Meanwhile, Schefter adds that once the wideout officially reports back to the 49ers, the team's options are to keep Aiyuk under his current contract, release him or look to move him ahead of this coming Tuesday's NFL trade deadline. Given the moving parts involved, it remains to be seen when Aiyuk might return to the field in any locale, but depending on his health and conditioning level, the 2020 first-rounder could represent an intriguing option for a team looking to add WR depth to consider.

items.head: Trending toward practicing Wednesday
items.body: Samuel (hamstring) is on track to return to practice Wednesday, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports. That's a positive development for Samuel, who logged a trio of 'DNPs' last week. His potential return this weekend against the Cowboys would be a welcome one for the 49ers' depleted WR corps. With that in mind, Mike Evans (Achilles) is viewed as iffy for the contest, so a key role in the team's passing attack could await Samuel if he is able to return for his first game action since Week 5.

items.head: Ruled out for Sunday
items.body: Samuel (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. Neither Samuel nor Mike Evans (Achilles) made a serious bid to play in San Francisco's first game after a Week 8 bye. Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing are the healthy WRs on the active roster, with Demarcus Robinson (ankle) a candidate to come off injured reserve this week or next.

items.head: Misses open portion of practice
items.body: Samuel (hamstring) didn't participate in the early portion of Friday's practice, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. With Samuel absent from the initial stage of practice Friday after sitting out Wednesday's and Thursday's sessions, he's trending toward an absence Sunday against the Raiders, as is fellow WR Mike Evans (Achilles). Confirmation of the duo's status is set to arrive later Friday once the 49ers' final Week 9 injury report is posted.

items.head: Not spotted Thursday
items.body: Samuel (hamstring) did not participate in the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. Samuel hasn't played or practiced since sustaining a hamstring injury in San Francisco's Week 5 win over the Seahawks. He'll likely require at least some ramp-up period upon returning to practice, and GM John Lynch indicated Thursday that Samuel is expected to sit out Sunday's game against the Raiders. Samuel's likely to be formally ruled out on Friday's injury report.

items.head: Not likely to play Sunday
items.body: According to GM John Lynch, Samuel (hamstring) is unlikely to be available for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports. The same applies to fellow WR Mike Evans (Achilles), but on the plus side for the 49ers, Demarcus Robinson (ankle) has been designated to return from IR and could be activated ahead of Week 9 action. In any case, the official game status' of the team's top two WRs will be clarified upon the release of Friday's injury report.

items.head: No practice Wednesday
items.body: Samuel (hamstring) won't take part in practice Wednesday, Cam Inman of The San Jose Mercury News reports. Samuel injured his right hamstring during a Week 5 win at Seattle, resulting in two missed games before the 49ers' Week 8 bye. Head coach Kyle Shanahan relayed to Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area on Oct. 26 that Samuel has a chance to return this Sunday against the Raiders, but Shanahan's tone was a bit different Wednesday, when he told Vic Tafur and Matt Barrows of The Athletic that Samuel doesn't seem as close to playing as fellow WR Mike Evans (Achilles).

items.head: Iffy for Wednesday's practice
items.body: Evans (Achilles) is unlikely to participate in practice Wednesday, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports. That's not a particularly surprising development, with Mike Garafolo of NFL Network having previously suggested that Evans -- who last played in Week 6 -- appears to be "questionable at best" for this Sunday's game against the Cowboys. On the plus side from the 49ers' perspective is that the team hopes to have fellow WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring) at practice Wednesday.

items.head: 'Questionable at best' for Week 10
items.body: Evans (Achilles), who won't play in Sunday's game against the Raiders, appears to be "questionable at best" for next Sunday's road matchup with the Cowboys, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. Evans is missing a second straight contest Sunday after aggravating a right Achilles injury during a Week 6 win against the Commanders. He hasn't been able to practice in the meantime, and while he's the type of player that doesn't require practice reps during the week to be available on game days, even work on the side Wednesday through Friday would be a welcome sign. In any case, with fellow WR Deebo Samuel (hamstring) also sidelined this weekend and Christian Kirk (knee) being placed on IR on Saturday, Demarcus Robinson, Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing and KhaDarel Hodge are the options at the position to be active in Week 9.

items.head: Won't play Sunday
items.body: Evans (Achilles) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Raiders, Nick Wagoner of ESPN reports. GM John Lynch said on KNBR radio Thursday that Evans is unlikely to play in Week 9 due to the right Achilles injury he aggravated in Week 6 against the Commanders, per Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area. After not practicing in any capacity Wednesday and Thursday, Evans indeed will miss a second consecutive contest. Fellow WRs Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (knee) will join Evans on the sideline Sunday, leaving Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing as the only options at the position on the 49ers' active roster. The team also may activate Demarcus Robinson (ankle) from IR on Saturday after he was listed as questionable.

items.head: Not seen at Friday's practice
items.body: Evans (Achilles) didn't participate in the portion of Friday's practice open to the media, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. With Evans now having been absent from the media-viewing portion of practice again Friday, his status for Sunday's game against the Raiders remains in serious doubt. After a round of likely DNPs, Evans' return may have to wait until Week 10, though the veteran wideout has been known to play despite logging DNPs. It could be another patchwork week at wide receiver for the Niners.

items.head: No practice Thursday
items.body: Evans (Achilles) didn't participate in Thursday's practice, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. After back-to-back DNPs to open Week 9 prep, Evans technically has one more chance to mix into drills this week, but GM John Lynch said on KNBR radio Thursday that the wide receiver likely won't be available Sunday versus the Raiders due to his lingering right Achilles issue, per Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area. The 49ers may make a ruling on Evans' status as soon as they post Friday's injury report.

items.head: Misses open portion Thursday
items.body: Evans (Achilles) didn't participate in the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. Evans' absence Thursday comes as no surprise considering GM John Lynch stated earlier in the day that Evans is unlikely to return Sunday against the Raiders. Barring an unexpectedly quick recovery, Evans will sit out a second consecutive game sandwiched around San Francisco's Week 8 bye before possibly returning in Week 10 at Dallas. At 6-1, the 49ers can afford to take a cautious approach with the top option in their injury-riddled wide receiver room.

items.head: Likely to sit Sunday per GM
items.body: Evans (Achilles) isn't expected to play Sunday against the Raiders, 49ers GM John Lynch said on KNBR radio Thursday, Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area reports. The 49ers were initially optimistic that Evans would return after the team's Week 8 bye following an absence during the Week 7 loss to Atlanta, but the veteran wide receiver apparently needs more time to recover. While official confirmation on Evans' status is unlikely to come prior to game designations being released Friday, Lynch's comments coupled with Evans' inability to practice Wednesday suggest that the wideout's fantasy managers should have an alternative option in place for Week 9.

items.head: Won't practice Wednesday
items.body: Head coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans (Achilles/ribs) won't practice Wednesday, NFL reporter Andrew Siciliano reports. Evans sat out a Week 7 loss in Atlanta after aggravating a right Achilles injury in Week 6 against the Commanders, and while there's an expectation that he'll be back after a Week 8 bye, he'll kick off this week with a DNP. He thus will have two more chances to mix into drills ahead of Sunday's contest versus the Raiders.

items.head: Could face season-ending elbow surgery
items.body: Per Adam Schefter of ESPN, Minshew (elbow) is reportedly seeking additional medical opinions to confirm that he likely will require season-ending surgery to address a torn UCL. Minshew's stint as the Cardinals' starting QB thus is shaping up to be a brief one. Assuming Schefter's report is confirmed, Carson Beck is slated to take over as Arizona's QB1, beginning with this Sunday's game against the Rams.

items.head: Gardner Minshew II (Elbow) is Doubtful
items.body: Per Adam Schefter of ESPN, Minshew (elbow) is reportedly seeking additional medical opinions to confirm that he likely will require season-ending surgery to address a torn UCL.

items.head: Set to undergo testing on arm/elbow
items.body: Minshew is slated to undergo testing on his right elbow/arm in the wake of Sunday's loss to the Seahawks, according to Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site. Minshew took over as the team's starting QB in advance of Week 9 action, and now his status for this weekend's game against the Rams is unclear. In the event that Minshew's issue ends up being long term, which could be a possibility, per Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com, Carson Beck is next in line for Arizona's signal-caller reps.

items.head: Sparse output in first Arizona start
items.body: Minshew was 21-for-30 passing for 166 yards, no touchdowns and no interceptions and had a four-yard carry during Sunday's 17-3 defeat in Seattle. Minshew was unable to recreate his magic from last Sunday's cameo in Dallas in which he put together four straight TD drives for the benched Jacoby Brissett to force overtime in an eventual 33-30 win. The series of events led head coach Mike LaFleur to announce Minshew as the Cardinals' new starting QB before the team finalized a trade to send Brissett to the Ravens. Minshew likely will be given some leash to help the offense generate more consistent results, but 2026 third-round pick Carson Beck is waiting in the wings in the event LaFleur opts to move on to the rookie.

items.head: Headed to injured reserve
items.body: Palmer (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Monday, Joe Buscaglia of the Athletic reports. In Palmer's absence, DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman will lead the Bills WR corps Monday night against the Vikings, with Greg Dortch and Trent Sherfield available in reserve. The earliest that Palmer can return to the mix is Sunday, Dec. 6 against the Patriots.

items.head: Won't play in Week 9
items.body: Palmer (hamstring) has been ruled out for Monday's game in Minnesota, Maddy Glab of the Bills' official site reports. Palmer exited last Sunday's win against the Ravens in the first half and wasn't able to return due to a hamstring injury. After not practicing Thursday or Friday, the Bills opted to keep him on the sidelines in Week 9, meaning Greg Dortch, Skyler Bell and/or Tyrell Shavers (knee, IR) may see WR reps behind the team's top trio at the position.

items.head: DNP on Thursday
items.body: Palmer (hamstring) did not practice Thursday. The veteran wideout was injured in Sunday's win over the Ravens and was unable to return to the contest. If he's unable to play Monday night against the Vikings, Skyler Bell and Greg Dortch could see additional work on offense.

items.head: Puka Nacua (Knee) is Doubtful
items.body: doubtful

items.head: IR stint appears likely
items.body: Coach Sean McVay indicated Monday that Nacua (knee) is likely headed to injured reserve with a PCL/MCL sprain and turf toe, Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register reports. With Davante Adams (hamstring) already on IR, Nacua's injury situation represents another huge blow to the Rams offense. Tutu Atwell, Konata Mumpfield, Jordan Whittington and CJ Daniels are the team's remaining healthy WRs, but a trade to bolster the position seems imperative ahead of Tuesday's deadline.

items.head: Will have MRI on knee Monday
items.body: Nacua suffered a knee injury during Sunday's 20-13 win at Washington and will undergo an MRI on Monday to determine its extent, Mike Garafolo of NFL Network reports. The Rams already are without WR Davante Adams for a few more weeks after he underwent surgery on his left hamstring, and the team now may be sans Nacua if the results of Monday's testing go a certain way. L.A. doesn't believe that Nacua sustained a torn ACL, but the MRI will reveal what type of damage he incurred. Before picking up the injury on the Rams' final offensive snap, Nacua gathered in 14 of 19 targets for 150 yards and one touchdown and took two carries for 20 yards.

items.head: Returns after brief exit
items.body: Nacua returned to Sunday's game against the Commanders after visiting the medical tent, Stu Jackson of the Rams' official site reports. Nacua was evaluated after sustaining an unspecified injury, but his absence wound up being brief. Barring another issue, he appears to be good to go for the remainder of Sunday's contest.

items.head: Michael Wilson (Neck) is Out
items.body: Coach Mike LaFleur revealed Monday that Wilson is out for the season due to a fracture in his neck, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Paces Cardinals in receiving
items.body: Wilson notched six catches (on seven targets) for 60 yards during Sunday's 17-3 loss in Seattle. Wilson has been tending to two broken ribs the last two games, and he also was working with new starting QB Gardner Minshew after the Cardinals dealt Jacoby Brissett to the Ravens this past week. Nonetheless, Wilson led Arizona in receiving yards, marking the fourth time he's reached 60 such yards in the last seven contests en route to a 38-412-2 line on 67 targets during that stretch. Wilson will look to improve his rapport with Minshew -- and also get healthier -- next Sunday versus the Rams.

items.head: No designation for Week 9
items.body: Wilson (rest/ribs) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's contest in Seattle, Josh Weinfuss of ESPN.com reports. Wilson has worn a yellow non-contact jersey in practice the last two weeks due to two broken ribs -- a situation that contained him to limited sessions. Having said that, he'll continue to play through the concern as he did this past Sunday in Dallas, when he hauled in eight of 15 targets for 111 yards and one touchdown while adding one carry for 17 yards on a 79 percent snap share.

items.head: Stays limited in practice
items.body: Wilson (rest/ribs) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Darren Urban of the Cardinals' official site reports. Wilson continues to don a yellow non-contact jersey on the practice field as he deals with two broken ribs, so his activity level comes as no surprise. Friday's injury report will determine if Wilson enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Seattle, but he's already demonstrated an ability to play through the issue, notching a 79 percent snap share, reeling in eight of 15 targets for 111 yards and one touchdown and recording a 17-yard carry in this past Sunday's win in Dallas.

items.head: Still in non-contact jersey
items.body: Wilson (ribs) remained in a yellow non-contact jersey at Thursday's practice, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports. Wilson has been wearing said jersey the past two weeks due to what he noted are two broken ribs. He still played through the pain this past Sunday in Dallas, despite exiting for a spell in the middle of the contest, ending Week 8 with eight catches (on 15 targets) for 111 yards and one touchdown and one carry for 17 yards. Thursday's injury report will unveil Wilson's activity level.

items.head: Stays limited Wednesday
items.body: Wilson (rest/ribs) practiced in a limited capacity Wednesday, Theo Mackie of The Arizona Republic reports. After Wilson continued to wear a yellow non-contact jersey at Wednesday's session, his ensuing activity level mimics what transpired last week, when he initially donned the jersey. He relayed after this past Sunday's win at Dallas that he has two broken ribs, but the addition of rest on the injury report this week indicates he's preparing to continue to play through the issue. Friday's practice report will reveal if Wilson has a designation for Sunday's game in Seattle.

items.head: Wearing non-contact jersey at practice
items.body: Wilson (ribs) wore a yellow non-contact jersey at Wednesday's practice, Bo Brack of GoPHNX.com reports. Wilson also donned such a jersey last week, when he was listed as limited on all three of the Cardinals' injury reports due to a rib injury. He then missed a spell from the second and into the third quarters this past Sunday in Dallas, after which it was revealed he's tending to two broken ribs. Wilson still put up an 8-111-1 line on 15 targets in that contest, and assuming he's able to suit up Sunday at Seattle, he'll be one of new starting QB Gardner Minshew's top available pass catchers along with TE Trey McBride.

items.body: Ahead of Week 10, Ravens head coach Jesse Minter noted "I expect (Brissett) to be our starter" next Monday against the Chargers, Jeff Zrebiec of The Athletic reports. Brissett officially landed with the Ravens in a trade with the Cardinals this past Friday, and he's now on track to assume his new team's starting QB role for the foreseeable future. As a result, Joe Fagnano -- who had a spot start in Week 9 -- will revert to backup status. With regard to franchise signal-caller Lamar Jackson (thumb), who currently is on IR, he's indicated that he plans to return later this season. However, he's out for at least three more games, and 4-5 Baltimore's record as the season progresses figures to factor into Jackson's approach to a potential return to action.

items.head: Shipped to Baltimore
items.body: The Ravens are finalizing a trade with the Cardinals that will send Brissett to Baltimore, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. The deal is expected to be completed over the weekend. Brissett was set to become a free agent this offseason and was demoted from the starting role earlier this week, making him an expendable piece for the Cardinals, who will move forward with Gardner Minshew and Carson Beck as their quarterbacks. Baltimore, meanwhile, had a critical need for an experienced signal-caller after losing  Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (foot) to injuries that will send both quarterbacks to injured reserve and potentially keep them out for the rest of the season, so Brissett will fill a void.
