Rice led the Chiefs in targets while finishing as the runner-up in both receptions and receiving yards. The veteran receiver has been busy the last two games while turning 15 targets into a 12-102-1 line, but he has just one catch of 20-plus yards in that span. Rice is averaging a relatively modest 11.7 yards per catch heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons.

items.head: Full participant Thursday
items.body: Rice (hamstring/knee) practiced without limitations Thursday. Rice is off the injury report Thursday after kicking off Week 9 prep with a limited session Wednesday. The oft-injured wide receiver has been limited to five appearances this season, one of which he left before recording a catch, but he has 20 catches for 243 yards and two touchdowns across the other four games. With Rice getting healthier, he could feast Sunday against a Jets defense that's allowing 30.7 points per game during an active three-game losing streak.

items.head: Limited Wednesday
items.body: Rice (hamstring/knee) was limited in Wednesday's practice. Rice got back in the fold in Week 8 to the tune of an 7-53-1 line after missing time with a hamstring injury, and he is limited to start preparation for the Jets. The Chiefs could be exercising caution with their top receiver, who also rehabbed from knee surgery during the offseason. A limited session Wednesday does not mean his Week 9 status is in jeopardy, but his participation over the coming days will be telling.

items.head: Team-high receiving yards in win
items.body: Kelce brought in four of six targets for 72 yards in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. He also rushed once for one yard. Kelce led the Chiefs in receiving yards and finished second in targets on the afternoon, and his tally in the former category also served as the legendary tight end's second highest of the season. Kelce got there with a big boost from a game-high 38-yard catch, and he'll take a formidable 33-482-2 line into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

items.head: Logs full practice Thursday
items.body: Kelce (ankle) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice. Kelce was deemed a limited participant Wednesday, but the tight end's full participation Thursday paves the way for him to be in uniform Sunday against the Jets. Over his last two games, the Chiefs' leader in catches and receiving yards has amassed nine catches (on 15 targets) for 111 yards with a TD, and as long as he stays healthy he'll merit weekly fantasy lineup consideration.

items.head: Limited practice Wednesday
items.body: Kelce (ankle) was listed as limited in Wednesday's practice. Kelce logged a limited session this past Thursday before practicing fully a day later. He then approached Week 8 action without an injury designation, en route to recording a 78 percent offensive snap share and catching five of his seven targets for 67 yards in the Chiefs' 28-24 loss to the Broncos. Chances are, the tight end's listed limitations Wednesday were maintenance-related, and he will now have two more chances to work fully ahead of Sunday's game against the Jets.

items.head: Two touches in Week 9 win
items.body: Williams brought in one of two targets for 31 yards and rushed once for nine yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Williams and the rest of the Lions' air attack had a quiet afternoon, as Jared Goff threw for just 170 yards overall. Williams was efficient on his two touches, but he finished with a new season low in receiving yards. The 2022 first-round pick, who's averaging 16.7 yards per reception on the season, will likely be busier in a Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

items.head: Just three grabs in Sunday's loss
items.body: Diggs caught three of five targets for 51 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo ended up leading the Commanders' injury-depleted group of pass catchers with seven targets each, and the former led the team in receiving yards and caught Jayden Daniels' only TD pass. Diggs' modest showing still represented his biggest yardage total since Week 1, although he did see his two-game scoring streak come to an end. Diggs will try to ramp up his production in Week 10 against the Giants.

items.head: Quiet day in Week 9 win
items.body: Goff completed 17 of 25 passes for 170 yards with no touchdowns and one interception while also rushing four times for five yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. Goff was the latest quarterback to scuffle some against a Dolphins defense that's fought hard all season, as the veteran signal-caller took three sacks and finished with a new season low in passing yards. Goff also failed to throw a touchdown for the first time this season, and he threw a pick for the second time in as many games after going without an interception for the first six contests of the campaign. Goff has completed at least 68.0 percent of his passes in three straight games heading into a Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany next Sunday.

items.head: Finds little running room in Week 9 loss
items.body: White carried the ball seven times for 28 yards and caught two of three targets for 41 yards in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. The 28 rushing yards led the Commanders on the afternoon, although Austin Ekeler saw one more carry than White did. With Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) set to miss at least one more contest while on IR, White seems likely to lead the backfield again in Week 10 against the Giants. Over the three games Croskey-Merritt has been sidelined so far, White has produced 186 scrimmage yards and two TDs -- one rushing and one receiving -- while averaging 4.4 yards per carry.

items.head: First turnover of season in loss to Rams
items.body: Daniels completed 24 of 35 passes for 274 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 20-13 loss to the Rams. He also gained 16 rushing yards on four carries and lost a fumble. The lost fumble was the first giveaway of the season for Daniels in six games. The third-year QB also struggled to sustain drives while working with a badly depleted wide receiver room, and his lone TD was a seven-yard toss to Van Jefferson -- a player who had zero catches on the year coming into Sunday -- in the second quarter. Injuries have derailed the first half of the season for the Commanders, but Daniels will try to spark his team to life in Week 10 against the Giants.

items.head: Logs 17 touches in Week 9 loss
items.body: Gordon rushed 16 times for 55 yards and brought in his only target for nine yards in the Dolphins' 19-9 loss to the Lions on Sunday. Gordon worked in the lead role as expected but found running room at a premium against a game Lions defense. Gordon has at least Sunday's carry total in four straight games, but he's now seen his rushing yardage total decline in consecutive games. Jaylen Wright's inactive status due to a quadriceps injury helped Gordon's touch floor overall, and the latter should remain the top option in Miami's ground attack in a favorable Week 10 road matchup against the Colts next Sunday.

items.head: Inefficient in lead role
items.body: Singletary rushed 21 times for 31 yards and caught two of three targets for eight yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. Singletary blew by his previous season high of six carries, as fellow running backs Cam Skattebo and Tyrone Tracy were both sidelined by hamstring injuries. Skattebo has a chance to return for Thursday's Week 10 matchup against the Commanders, while Tracy won't be back prior to Week 12, so Singletary is likely to maintain an elevated role unless the Giants trade for another running back prior to Tuesday's deadline. Singletary didn't make the most of his added opportunities against the Eagles, averaging a meager 1.5 yards per carry.

items.head: Ticketed for RB1 duties
items.body: With Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doubtful to play Week 9, Singletary is expected to operate as the Giants' lead back Sunday against the Eagles, Jordan Raanan of ESPN.com reports. Tyrone Tracy (hamstring) is on injured reserve and required to miss at least the next four games, and Najee Harris was recently released, so it'll be Singletary's job Sunday. Practice-squad types Greg Desrosiers and Phil Mafah are in tow as the backups but both have little-to-no experience carrying the ball in the NFL. Volume alone will put Singletary in the fantasy RB2 mix.

items.head: Hits paydirt against Washington
items.body: Corum carried the ball 11 times for 58 yards and a touchdown and failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. The Rams' backfield has become a full-fledged timeshare, with Corum getting double-digit carries for a third straight game and out-producing Kyren Williams on the ground in Washington. Corum has gotten into the end zone in all three of those contests, punching in a one-yard score in the third quarter Sunday, and over that stretch he's amassed 224 rushing yards and three TDs while averaging 5.7 yards a carry. With Puka Nacua (knee) headed for an MRI, the Rams could lean even more heavily on their ground attack in a Week 10 tilt against the Cardinals.

items.head: Another 300-yard tally in win
items.body: Prescott completed 21 of 34 passes for 335 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions while rushing twice for one yard in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Prescott had a couple of bumps in the road against an inconsistent Colts defense, but the veteran signal-caller, who was also working without George Pickens (hamstring), still found his way to his third 300-yard effort of the season. Prescott unsurprisingly bestowed plenty of attention on CeeDee Lamb, who ultimately was responsible for 10 of his completions, 195 of his yards and one of his two TDs. Prescott also connected with Jake Ferguson for a 10-yard scoring strike early in the second quarter, and the one blemish on the star quarterback's day was a  fumble on a sack at his own 16-yard line that led to a Colts touchdown. Prescott has at least one touchdown pass in every game heading into

items.head: Just one TD in Week 9 win
items.body: Stafford completed 26 of 43 passes for 228 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 20-13 win over the Commanders. He added one yard on his only carry. The veteran QB looked the way of Puka Nacua (knee) early and often, with no other Ram pass catcher managing more than 20 receiving yards, and the star wideout was on the other end of a seven-yard TD toss in the fourth quarter that proved to be the winning score. Stafford has thrown a single touchdown pass in back-to-back games after producing multiple TDs in five of six contests before that, and his options could get even thinner with Nacua headed for an MRI after getting hurt on L.A.'s final possession.

items.head: Practices fully Wednesday
items.body: Stafford (right elbow) was a full participant in Wednesday's practice, Sarah Barshop of ESPN reports. Stafford was seen leaving the locker room with his upper right arm wrapped in ice after this past Sunday's win against the Chargers. Head coach Sean McVay told Adam Grosbard of The Orange County Register on Monday that Stafford has been tending to arm soreness, but the quarterback clarified the situation with Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times on Wednesday, stating that he's had his right arm wrapped in ice regularly this season. An uncapped session to begin Week 9 prep puts Stafford in the clear to continue to lead the Ramas offense Sunday in Washington.

items.head: Eclipses century mark in win
items.body: Williams rushed 20 times for 101 yards and a touchdown and brought in four of five targets for 23 yards in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. Williams turned in one of his more efficient performances against an inconsistent Colts defense, ultimately managing his second 100-yard effort of the season. Williams continued to serve as a prolific supplier of touchdowns as well, recording his ninth rushing score of the campaign on a one-yard run with 1:08 remaining to seal the victory for Dallas. Williams' week-to-week yardage production has fluctuated a fair amount, but his high-volume role and trusted red-zone presence keeps him a must-play despite a tough Week 10 home matchup against the 49ers next Sunday.

items.head: Standout numbers again in win
items.body: Lamb brought in 10 of 16 targets for 195 yards and a touchdown in the Cowboys' 27-23 win over the Colts on Sunday. He also lost a fumble. Lamb easily led the Cowboys across the board in receptions, receiving yards and targets in a game that Dallas was operating without George Pickens (hamstring). Lamb's yardage total was a new season high, and he rounded out his stellar day with his seventh touchdown catch of the campaign on a 44-yard grab just before halftime. Even his turnover had a bright side to it from a fantasy perspective, as Lamb gained 44 yards on an impressive downfield catch and picked up extra yardage after the Colts initially failed to touch him down before fumbling at the end of that sequence. Lamb has four straight double-digit target games and is just 96 yards away from his sixth consecutive 1,000-yard season h

items.head: Bottled up by Commanders
items.body: Williams carried the ball 15 times for 45 yards and caught three of four targets for 16 yards in Sunday's 20-13 win over Washington. Blake Corum was the more productive Ram on the ground, turning 11 carries into 58 yards and a touchdown, but the offense mainly flowed through Puka Nacua on the afternoon. Williams failed to find the end zone for only the third time in nine games this season, and the 45 rushing yards were his lowest total since Week 1, although he has yet to reach 100 in any contest. The Los Angeles backfield has become a clear timeshare however, limiting Williams' upside heading into a Week 10 trip to Arizona.

items.head: Three total TDs in win
items.body: Walker rushed 18 times for 102 yards and a touchdown and brought in all four targets for 41 yards and two more scores in the Chiefs' 35-12 win over the Jets on Sunday. Walker put together another one of his signature high-efficiency performances on the ground, averaging 5.7 yards per carry in the process. He contributed a seven-yard touchdown reception on the first play of the second quarter, and he struck again as a receiver via a 25-yard scoring grab with just over five minutes remaining in the first half. Walker capped off the highly fantasy-friendly day with his seventh rushing touchdown of the season, a two-yard run in the waning moments of the third quarter. Walker is up to 872 rushing yards, 172 receiving yards and 11 total touchdowns heading into a Week 10 road matchup against the Falcons next Sunday.

items.head: Suffers injury setback at practice
items.body: Coach Sean McVay noted Sunday that Ferguson pulled his hamstring during Friday's practice and will likely be sidelined for another couple of weeks, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports. Ferguson, who had previously been out with an ankle injury, was designated to return from IR on Wednesday and on the verge of a return to the Rams' lineup prior to Friday's setback. With that in mind, McVay said that the tight end was going to be a "big part" of the game plan Sunday against the Commanders. Instead, Tyler Higbee (one catch for 13 yards on five targets) and Colby Parkinson (four catches on any many targets for 13) yards) were the team's primary pass-catching options at the TE position in Week 9.

items.head: Terrance Ferguson (Hamstring) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Coach Sean McVay noted Sunday that Ferguson pulled his hamstring during Friday's practice and will likely be sidelined for another couple of weeks, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Suffers hamstring injury, out again
items.body: Ferguson (ankle) was expected to return for Sunday's game against Washington, but he's been ruled out after injuring his hamstring during Friday's practice, Cameron DaSilva of USA Today reports. Ferguson made it back from his ankle injury, only to be sidelined by another concern two days before he was set for a return to game action. The Rams could use him, as they haven't found a second consistent receiving threat alongside Puka Nacua in the absence of Davante Adams (IR - hamstring). Another absence for Ferguson leaves Tyler Higbee as well as  Colby Parkinson (ribs, questionable), if available, as the Rams' tight top ends, with Davis Allen and Max Klare providing extra bodies for multi-TE sets.

items.head: No injury designation
items.body: Ferguson (ankle) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Commanders, Adam Caplan of SiriusXM NFL Radio reports. The tight end is expected to be activated from injured reserve Saturday afternoon and make his return to the lineup Sunday. With Davante Adams (hamstring) out several more weeks, Ferguson has a big opportunity to essentially serve as the Rams' WR2, putting him in the mix as a fantasy starter at tight end.

items.head: In line to return Sunday
items.body: Head coach Sean McVay said Friday that Ferguson (ankle) is expected to play in Sunday's game at Washington, Sarah Barshop of ESPN.com reports. Since the Rams designated Ferguson for return from injured reserve Wednesday, he's managed a pair of limited practices as he works his way back from an ankle sprain that he suffered in Week 3 at Denver. He seems destined to be listed as questionable for Week 9 action, and then the team must activate him from IR by Saturday afternoon for him to have a chance to suit up Sunday.

items.head: Stays limited Thursday
items.body: Ferguson (ankle) was a limited practice participant Thursday, Greg Beacham of the Associated Press reports. Ferguson has been sidelined since spraining his ankle in Week 3 at Denver, missing the last five games a result. The Rams designated him for return from injured reserve Wednesday, and he's managed two limited sessions since then. Friday's practice report will determine if Ferguson has a chance to return to action Sunday in Washington, but he'll still need to be activated from IR by Saturday afternoon to be in a position to do so.

items.head: Officially limited Wednesday
items.body: Ferguson (ankle) was limited in Wednesday's practice. The Rams opened Ferguson's 21-day practice window Wednesday, as he looks to return from injured reserve for Sunday's game against the Commanders. If Colby Parkinson (ribs) is unable to play for the second straight week, Ferguson would join Tyler Higbee and Davis Allen at tight end for Los Angeles.

items.head: Practice window opens Wednesday
items.body: Ferguson (ankle) is returning to practice Wednesday, opening his 21-day window to return, Gary Klein of the LA Times reports. Ferguson has been out since sustaining an ankle injury against the Broncos in Week 3. He has upward of 21 days to be activated off IR. A return in Week 9 may be optimistic at this stage and will hinge on his practice participation for the remainder of the week. Regardless, Ferguson is trending toward being back on the field in the near future.

items.head: Eight catches in Week 9 win
items.body: St. Brown brought in eight of 10 targets for 86 yards in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. St. Brown set the pace across the board for the Lions in receptions, receiving yards and targets. St. Brown was playing through a rib issue that had limited him throughout the practice week, but he turned in an efficient effort that included his fifth straight game with six or more catches. St. Brown's touchdown drought did extend to five games, and he'll once again aim to snap it in next Sunday's Week 10 matchup against the Patriots in Germany.

items.head: Active for Sunday's game
items.body: St. Brown (ribs) is active for Sunday's game in Miami. St. Brown tended to a rib injury during Week 9 prep that limited him in all three sessions and left him questionable ahead of the weekend. Having said that, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reported Sunday morning that St. Brown was expected to play, which now has been confirmed. St. Brown will be taking on a Dolphins defense that has allowed an NFL-worst 9.8 yards per target to opposing wide receivers this season.

items.head: In line to play Sunday
items.body: St. Brown (ribs) is slated to play in Sunday's game at Miami, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. St. Brown was forced from last Sunday's win against the Vikings for a spell due to an undisclosed injury, but he was able to return and finished with seven catches (on eight targets) for 46 yards and a 10-yard carry. He then was limited at Wednesday's walkthrough due to a rib issue and followed it up with back-to-back capped sessions before being tagged as questionable for Week 9 action. Ultimately, St. Brown's status will be confirmed about 90 minutes before Sunday's 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff.

items.head: Listed questionable for Sunday
items.body: St. Brown (ribs) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Dolphins, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports. After a round of limited practices this week, St. Brown's status for Sunday is in question. It's worth wondering if the Lions could sit the star wideout against a perceived inferior opponent to help his ribs heal. If St. Brown does miss Sunday's game, Jameson Williams and Isaac TeSlaa would play every-down roles at wide receiver, with Sam LaPorta possibly benefiting the most as the player who runs his routes in the same area of the field as St. Brown.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: St. Brown (ribs) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports. St. Brown maintained his activity level from Wednesday's walkthrough as he navigates a rib injury, which was likely the reason for his brief time on the sideline this past Sunday against the Vikings. He thus has one more chance to get back to full Friday, or else he'll be at risk of entering the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Miami.

items.head: Limited at Wednesday's walkthrough
items.body: St. Brown was a limited participant at Wednesday's walkthrough due to a rib injury, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports. St. Brown made a brief exit during this past Sunday's win against the Vikings due to an undisclosed injury but was able to return, finishing with seven catches (on eight targets) for 46 yards and one carry for 10 yards. The nature of the health concern has been revealed, but his ability to practice in some capacity Wednesday generally bodes well for his status ahead of Sunday's game at Miami.

items.head: Rush TD in Week 9 win
items.body: Gibbs rushed 20 times for 74 yards and a touchdown and failed to bring in his only target in the Lions' 19-9 win over the Dolphins on Sunday. It was a relatively quiet day by Gibbs' lofty standards against a Dolphins team that's proven to have plenty of fight despite its losing record. The standout back salvaged his fantasy day with an eight-yard touchdown run late in the third quarter, Gibbs' second score on the ground in as many games and ninth overall. Gibbs failed to record at least one reception for the first time this season, but he's already amassed 1,132 scrimmage yards and 11 total touchdowns across eight games heading into next Sunday's showdown against the Patriots in Germany.

items.head: Bottled up outside of short TD
items.body: Barkley rushed 13 times for 22 yards and a touchdown while failing to catch his only target in Sunday's 19-11 loss to the Giants. Barkley has mustered a meager 2.0 yards per carry over the past two games while playing through hamstring and back injuries, but he also has both of Philadelphia's touchdowns over that span, including a three-yard rushing score in the second quarter Sunday. It has been a slog offensively for the Eagles, who have tried first Tanner McKee and now Joe Milton under center since losing starting QB Jalen Hurts (IR, calf) likely for the season while also playing without top two wide receivers DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle). It's fair to wonder if Barkley will eventually be shut down as well to get a chance to heal as the 2-7 Eagles drop out of contention, but at least a Week

items.head: Clear for Week 9 action
items.body: Barkley (hamstring/back) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. After sitting out Wednesday's session due to lingering hamstring and back injuries, Barkley ended Week 9 prep with back-to-back limited practices, which was enough to get the all-clear ahead of Sunday. He gutted out a 32 percent snap share this past Sunday in Washington en route to 14 touches for 54 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD while splitting the backfield with Elijah Mitchell (15 touches for 37 total yards).

items.head: Practicing again Friday
items.body: Barkley (hamstring/back) is practicing again Friday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports. After logging a limited practice Thursday, Barkley was back on the field again Friday as he continues to manage hamstring and back issues ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants. His official participation level and final injury designation will provide the clearest read on his Week 9 availability.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Barkley (hamstring/back) practiced in a limited capacity Thursday. Barkley followed up Wednesday's DNP with some activity one day later as he deals with lingering hamstring and back injuries. Friday's practice report will determine if he enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game against the Giants. While playing through those health concerns this past Sunday in Washington, Barkley logged a 32 percent snap share and racked up 14 touches for 54 yards from scrimmage and one rushing TD.

items.head: Practicing Thursday
items.body: Barkley (hamstring/back) is participating in Thursday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports. After sitting out Wednesday's practice due to existing hamstring and back injuries, Barkley is returning to drills one day later, which is one day earlier than a week ago. He thus appears to be a bit healthier this time around, but his activity level will become known once the Eagles post their second Week 9 practice report Thursday.

items.head: Not spotted at practice
items.body: Barkley wasn't present for the media-access portion of Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports. Barkley may still be tending to the hamstring and back issues that he impacted his practice reps last week, but Wednesday's injury report will reveal if he indeed was a non-participant and also the reason for his absence. Jaydon Blue is the only healthy RB on the Eagles' active roster, though practice-squad member Elijah Mitchell tallied 11 carries for 34 yards and four catches (on six targets) for three yards while splitting the backfield with Barkley this past Sunday at Washington.

items.head: Quiet in Week 9 win
items.body: Nabers caught five of eight targets for 43 yards in Sunday's 19-11 win over the Eagles. Nabers recorded at least 111 receiving yards in four consecutive games prior to the Giants' Week 8 bye but failed to extend that streak in Sunday's low-scoring win, during which J.J. McCarthy (hip) and Jameis Winston combined to throw for just 198 yards. The star wide receiver led the team with eight targets but finished third in receiving yards behind Darnell Mooney (54) and Isaiah Likely (53). Nabers had his hands on what would have been a 20-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter but failed to secure a diving catch attempt. McCarthy left in the third quarter but managed to return later in the second half, and he can be tentatively penciled in as the starting QB for Thursday's home game agai

items.head: Ready for Sunday
items.body: Nabers (knee) doesn't have a designation for Sunday's game in Philadelphia. Nabers was held out of drills Thursday due to a knee injury, but his return to all activity one day later lines up with head coach John Harbaugh's assessment of the situation Friday, when he told Matt Citak of the Giants' official site that the wide receiver "practiced fully" and is "full go" for Week 9. As a result, Nabers will look to build upon the massive 36-509-2 line on 51 targets that he's accrued over the last four contests.

items.head: 'Full go' for Week 9
items.body: Head coach John Harbaugh said Nabers (knee) "practiced fully" Friday and will be "full go" for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Matt Citak of the Giants' official site reports. That's not to say Nabers won't be tagged with a designation once the Giants post their final Week 9 injury report Friday, but it appears his absence from Thursday's practice due to a knee issue was merely a blip on the radar. He's strung together four consecutive 100-yard performances, a stretch in which his receiving line sits at 36-509-2 on 51 targets. Nabers' presence will be key for New York's offense led by J.J. McCarthy, who will be making his second start of the season since assuming the Giants' QB1 role.

items.head: Looks ready for Sunday
items.body: Nabers (knee) was catching passes during Friday's walkthrough and should be "good" to go For Sunday's game against the Eagles, Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post reports. After sitting out Thursday's practice due to the knee issue, Nabers appears to be trending in the right direction for Sunday's game at Philadelphia. Still, the Giants' final injury report will provide the clearest indication of whether the wide receiver takes a designation into the weekend.

items.head: DNP due to knee injury
items.body: Nabers didn't practice Thursday due to a knee injury, Dan Salomone of the Giants' official site reports. Nabers opened Thursday's session working on the side with trainers, and afterward he told Art Stapleton of USA Today, "I'll be good," as it pertains to his status for Week 9. In any case, the reason for Nabers' absence is a knee issue, which could be related to the right ACL tear that ended his 2025 season in Week 4. He'll have one more chance to prove his health Friday, at which point the Giants may tag him with a designation for Sunday's game in Philadelphia.

items.head: Offers positive update
items.body: Nabers (undisclosed) said Thursday, "I'll be good," for Sunday's game at Philadelphia, Art Stapleton of USA Today reports. Nabers was spotted working with the Giants' training staff during the media-access portion of Thursday's practice, one day removed from not being on the team's initial Week 9 injury report. The reason for his likely practice restrictions isn't known but will be revealed once New York posts its second injury report of the week.

items.head: Spotted with training staff Thursday
items.body: Nabers had his jersey and helmet on but worked with the Giants' training staff during the portion of Thursday's practice open to the media, Pat Leonard of the New York Daily News reports. Nabers may be dealing with an injury ahead of Sunday's game against the Eagles, so Thursday's injury report will be worth monitoring, as that will reveal the extent of Nabers' practice participation as well as the nature of any injuries that may be bothering the star wide receiver. He was on a roll prior to the Giants' Week 8 bye, recording at least 111 receiving yards in four consecutive games.

items.head: Gets 18 touches in return
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) rushed 15 times for 61 yards and caught three of four targets for 26 yards in Sunday's 35-12 loss to the Chiefs. Hall reclaimed the lead role in his first action since Week 3, notching 87 yards on 18 touches compared to 54 yards and a lost fumble on 10 touches for Braelon Allen. The 25-year-old Hall has racked up at least 16 touches in all four of his appearances this season, and the 22-year-old Allen's four consecutive games over 100 scrimmage yards entering Sunday's action weren't enough to pry the starting role away from Hall. Expect Hall to continue leading the backfield in Week 10 against the Bills, with his superior receiving ability likely to come into play if the 2-7 Jets fall behind as expected.

items.head: Looks like Sunday starter
items.body: Based on pregame warmups, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic suggests that it seems like Hall will start at RB for the Jets in Sunday's game against the Chiefs. Hall, who hasn't seen game action since sustaining a quad injury in Week 3, approached Sunday's contest minus an injury designation, thus setting him up to rejoin a Jets backfield that had been capably paced by Braelon Allen in his absence. While it looks like Hall is set to reclaim his key role in the team's backfield, offensive coordinator Frank Reich said Thursday the Jets intend to utilize "a mix" of the two running backs Sunday, per Al Iannazzone of Newsday Sports, an approach that makes sense given how well Allen has produced of late.

items.head: Expected to play Sunday
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) "has been medically cleared" and is expected to play Sunday against the Chiefs, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Hall has not taken the field since sustaining a quad injury in Week 3, but he practiced fully Thursday and appears primed to return to action Sunday. Braelon Allen has shined in Hall's absence, but Hall entered the season as the starter, so both figure to be involved to some degree in Week 9.

items.head: Practices fully Thursday
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) was a full participant in Thursday's practice. After opening the week with a limited session, Hall upgraded to full participation Thursday, indicating that he's in the clear to return Sunday against the Chiefs for his first action since Week 3. Braelon Allen has thrived in the lead role during Hall's absence, and offensive coordinator Frank Reich said Thursday that the Jets intend to utilize "a mix" of the two running backs Sunday, per Al Iannazzone of Newsday Sports. Hall is the superior receiving back, but Allen is averaging 5.0 yards per carry while Hall averaged just 3.2 YPC prior to getting hurt.

items.head: Says he's ready to go this week
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) indicated Thursday that he's ready to play Sunday against the Chiefs, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports. Hall, who hasn't played since Sept. 27, participated in Thursday's practice, though it remains to be seen if the Jets list him as a full or limited participant. In any case, the running back is trending toward a return to action this weekend, and if he is indeed available versus Kansas City, Hall will rejoin a backfield that's been capably paced paced by Braelon Allen in his absence.

items.head: Practicing again Thursday
items.body: Hall (quadriceps) is participating in Thursday's practice, Rich Cimini of ESPN.com reports. Hall, who was a limited participant at Wednesday's practice session, was also limited throughout the week leading up to the Jets' Week 8 loss to the Raiders, which the running back sat out. While the team's coaching staff has expressed optimism that Hall will be ready to return Sunday against the Chiefs, his status will remain up in the air until he's able to practice without limitations. Thursday's participation level has yet to be revealed, but Hall's presence at practice suggests that he has at least avoided a setback.

items.head: Set for limited practice Wednesday
items.body: Jets head coach Aaron Glenn said that Hall (quadriceps) will be a limited practice participant Wednesday, Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic reports. Hall, who hasn't played since Sept. 27, was also limited at practice last week, but Glenn said that the running back is "trending in the right direction" as Sunday's game against the Chiefs approaches, per Rich Cimini of ESPN.com. As for how the workload might be split between Hall and Braelon Allen should Hall return this weekend, Glenn declined to go in specifics beyond noting that "both will play" in such a scenario, according to Cimini.

items.head: Mo Alie-Cox (Groin) is Questionable
items.body: Alie-Cox is questionable to return to Sunday's game against Dallas due to a groin injury.

items.head: Jonathan Mingo (Ankle) is Questionable
items.body: Mingo (ankle) is questionable to return to Sunday's matchup against the Colts, Patrik Walker of the Cowboys' official site reports.

items.head: Inactive in Week 9
items.body: Lloyd (knee) is listed as inactive Sunday at New England, Mike Spofford of the Packers' official site reports. The Packers added Lloyd to the Week 9 injury report Thursday as limited due to a knee injury, and he maintained that activity level Friday before the team tagged him as questionable ahead of the weekend. Now that Lloyd is confirmed to be unavailable, Pierre Strong and Kaleb Johnson will be the team's complementary backfield options behind No. 1 option Josh Jacobs.

items.head: Questionable for Week 9
items.body: Lloyd (knee) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Patriots. Lloyd was added to the injury report Thursday, which is rarely a good sign for a player's availability Sunday. If Lloyd can't play, Pierre Strong figures to draw in as the pass-catching complement to Josh Jacobs out of the Packers' backfield.

items.head: Dealing with knee issue
items.body: Lloyd was limited at practice Thursday due to a knee injury. Lloyd's addition to the Packers' practice report midweek is something to monitor, especially because it may indicate a health concern that occurred during Thursday's session. Ultimately, Friday's injury report may provide some clarity into the situation.

items.head: Returns to lineup Sunday
items.body: Hollins (calf) is listed as active for Sunday's game against the Packers. Hollins, who had landed on IR prior to Week 5 action, was activated from IR/designated to return Saturday but still carried a 'questionable' designation ahead of the contest. In his first game action since Week 4, Hollins could make an immediate contribution to a WR corps that also includes DeMario Douglas, Efton Chism and Kyle Williams, but remains without A.J. Brown (knee/ankle) and Romeo Doubs (IR, shoulder). Prior to his injury, Hollins recorded a 15/209/0 receiving line on 20 targets through four games.

items.head: Questionable for Week 9
items.body: Hollins (calf) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Packers. The Patriots would need to activate Hollins from injured reserve by 4 p.m. ET on Saturday to have him available for Sunday's game against the Packers. The team could certainly use him with A.J. Brown (knee) out again, but Hollins never made it back to full practice participation, instead logging limited sessions Wednesday through Friday.

items.head: Limited in return to practice
items.body: Hollins (calf) was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice after being designated for return from injured reserve. After the Patriots opened up his 21-day evaluation window, Hollins took the field for his first practice since Week 4. Hollins will be eligible for activation from IR at any point, but unless he upgrades to full participation by the end of the week, he could have a tough time gaining clearance for Sunday's matchup with the Packers. Through New England's first four games before he sustained a calf injury, Hollins produced a 15-209-0 receiving line on 20 targets.

items.head: Set to resume practicing Wednesday
items.body: The Patriots are expected to designate Hollins (calf) for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Hollins' last game appearance came back in Week 4, but with his return to practice on the horizon, he could be an option for the Patriots as soon as this Sunday's game against the Packers. With Romeo Doubs (shoulder) currently on IR and A.J. Brown's (ankle/knee) availability for Week 9 looking cloudy, Hollins could have a chance at claiming a meaningful role right off the bat if he's cleared to play versus Green Bay. Prior to sustaining the calf injury, Hollins logged a 15-209-0 receiving line on 20 targets through New England's first four games.

items.head: Three grabs in Sunday's loss
items.body: Pitts caught three of five targets for 23 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. It was another quiet performance from Pitts, who hasn't reached 25 receiving yards in any of the last three games, and he had to watch backup tight end Charlie Woerner catch Michael Penix's only TD pass of the afternoon in the first quarter. Pitts will take a 25-220-4 line on 37 targets through nine contests into a Week 10 clash with Kansas City.

items.head: Will Kacmarek (Quadriceps) is Questionable
items.body: Kacmarek is dealing with a quad injury and is questionable to return to Sunday's clash against Detroit.

items.head: Held in check through air by Bengals
items.body: Penix completed 20 of 31 passes for 162 yards and a touchdown with an interception in Sunday's 34-17 loss to Cincinnati. He added 50 rushing yards on three carries. It looked like it would be a big day for the Falcons offense when Penix led his team to points on its first two drives. including a one-yard TD to Charlie Woerner, but Atlanta managed just seven more points over the final three quarters. The touchdown pass was Penix's 10th of the season, setting a new career high, but he's also been picked off five times in the last two games after throwing only one INT in his first five contests of 2026. He'll face a tough test in Week 10 against Kansas City.

items.head: Ruled out for rest of Sunday's game
items.body: Waddle (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports. After being evaluated for a potential concussion, Waddle is done for the day and will thus target a potential return to action Nov. 22 against the Raiders, following Denver's Week 10 bye. In his absence Sunday, Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims will handle the team's WR duties versus Carolina.

items.head: Jaylen Waddle (Concussion) is Questionable
items.body: Waddle (concussion) has been ruled out for the remainder of Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports.

items.head: Being checked for concussion
items.body: Waddle is being evaluated for a potential concussion during Sunday's game against the Panthers, Parker Gabriel of The Denver Post reports. Per Chris Tomasson of the Denver Gazette, Waddle headed to the locker room Sunday after having absorbed a hard hit, leaving  Courtland Sutton, Pat Bryant, Troy Franklin and Marvin Mims as the Broncos' available WRs. Prior to his exit, Waddle caught his only target for 22 yards.

items.head: Leading receiver in Week 9 loss
items.body: London caught all five of his targets for 68 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Cincinnati's secondary did a good job of limiting London's looks from Michael Penix, but the fifth-year wideout still led Atlanta in receiving yards, although Bijan Robinson caught one more pass and Charlie Woerner hauled in the QB's only touchdown. London has gotten only 11 targets over the last two games, turning them into a disappointing 6-76-0 line, and he could have a hard time breaking out in Week 10 against a stingy Kansas City secondary.

items.head: Big workload in loss to Cincy
items.body: Robinson carried the ball 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown and caught six of seven targets for 47 yards in Sunday's 34-17 loss to the Bengals. Backup Khalil Herbert handled just three touches, as Robinson dominated the workload in the Atlanta backfield with his usual No. 2, Brian Robinson (hamstring), on the shelf. It was the first time since Week 4 that Bijan had reached the century mark in rushing yards, and also the first time since that game against the Saints he got into the end zone. Robinson will look to build upon this effort in Week 10 against Kansas City.

items.head: Quiet in Week 9 win
items.body: Brown carried the ball nine times for 57 yards and caught all three of his targets for 18 yards in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. Samaje Perine actually saw more volume on the ground with 11 carries for 43 yards, but most of his workload came in the fourth quarter as the Bengals were grinding down the clock. Brown has yet to top 80 rushing yards in a game this season and he hasn't gotten into the end zone since Week 1, a disappointing first half of the year for a running back who amassed at least 1,300 scrimmage yards with double-digit scores each of the prior two campaigns. Brown will look for an opportunity to break out in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.

items.head: Finds end zone twice in win over Falcons
items.body: Higgins caught five of six targets for 32 yards and two touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over Atlanta. While he didn't see big volume, Higgins made his opportunities count, connecting with Joe Burrow on a four-yard TD in the second quarter and an eight-yard score in the third. Higgins has hit paydirt five times in the last three games, and on the season he's produced a 48-758-6 line on 67 targets through eight contests. He'll look to extend his scoring streak in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North clash with the Steelers.

items.head: Dominates in Madrid
items.body: Chase caught 10 of 12 targets for 155 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. The superstar wideout hit the ground running in Madrid, capping Cincinnati's first drive with a 47-yard touchdown catch from Joe Burrow. It was Chase's fourth straight game getting into the end zone, a stretch in which he's delivered a stellar 32-435-4 line on 45 targets, and Sunday's 155 receiving yards were a season high. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 during a crucial AFC North battle against the Steelers.

items.head: Another stellar effort in Week 9 win
items.body: Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards and three touchdowns in Sunday's 34-17 win over the Falcons. He added seven yards and a TD on three carries. It was a nearly flawless performance from Burrow, as he hit Ja'Marr Chase for a 47-yard score in the first quarter and tossed a pair of shorter TDs to Tee Higgins later in the contest. The superstar QB also got into the end zone on a goal-line sneak in the second quarter. It's the fourth straight game in which Burrow has produced at least four touchdowns, an incredible stretch in which he's completed 77.0 percent of his passes for 1,215 yards with a 16:3 TD:INT plus two more scores on the ground. The Bengals, not coincidentally, are 4-0 in that span. Burrow will look to stay locked in for a big AFC North clash against the Steelers in Week 10.

items.head: Not activated ahead of Week 9
items.body: Njoku (fibula) wasn't activated from IR-designated to return ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, per the NFL's official transaction log. Njoku returned to practice this week but was limited all three days before being deemed doubtful for Week 9 action. The TE's next chance to play will arrive Monday, Nov. 16, when the Chargers face the Ravens.

items.head: David Njoku (Lower Leg) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Njoku (fibula) wasn't activated from IR-designated to return ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans, per the NFL's official transaction log.

items.head: Doubtful for Sunday
items.body: Njoku (fibula) is listed as doubtful for Sunday's game against the Texans. Njoku returned to practice this week but never advanced from limited participation to full. He could have a real shot next week when the Chargers face the Ravens. In the meantime, Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden will get most of the TE snaps for Los Angeles.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Njoku (fibula) was limited in Thursday's practice. Njoku had his 21-day practice window opener Wednesday, and he's logged back-to-back limited practice sessions to begin Week 9 work. He's been on the shelf since going down with the lower leg injury in Week 2.

items.head: Cleared to resume practicing
items.body: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh said Wednesday that Njoku (fibula) has been designated for return from injured reserve, Alex Insdorf of BoltBeat.com reports. The transaction opens up a 21-day window wherein Njoku can be evaluated for a return to the 53-man roster. The veteran tight end has been out of action since sustaining the fibula injury Week 2, but if he's able to turn in a full practice at some point over the next three days, he could have a chance at being activated from IR ahead of Sunday's game against the Texans. Once he's back in the fold, Njoku could push Charlie Kolar and Oronde Gadsden for snaps at tight end.

items.head: Active for Week 9
items.body: Vaki (ankle) is available for Sunday's game against Miami. Vaki didn't practice Friday, resulting in a questionable tag for Week 9. However, he will be out there against the Dolphins and may continue to be more involved after totaling 11 carries in the Week 8 win over the Vikings.

items.head: Inactive in Week 9
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) is listed as inactive Sunday against the Lions. After sitting out Wednesday's practice due to a quadriceps injury, Wright was able to get back to limited Thursday and maintain that activity level Friday, at which point he was tagged as questionable in advance of the weekend. On Sunday morning, however, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reported that Wright wasn't expected to suit up, and that's now locked in. With Wright out of the lineup, Kaytron Allen (quad) and Carlos Washington will serve as the reserve RB options behind Ollie Gordon.

items.head: Not slated to play Sunday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) isn't in line to play in Sunday's game against the Lions, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Wright was held out of drills Wednesday due to a quad injury before capping Week 9 prep with back-to-back limited practices. That left him questionable to suit up Sunday, but assuming he's listed among the Dolphins' inactives about 90 minutes before a 1:00 p.m. ET kickoff, he'll be in street clothes this weekend. Kaytron Allen (quadriceps, questionable) and Carlos Washington are the other options to handle complementary reps behind No. 1 RB Ollie Gordon.

items.head: Deemed questionable
items.body: Wright (quad) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Lions, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Averaging just 1.9 yards per carry, Wright is unlikely to get more than a handful of touches off the bench if he's active this Sunday. Ollie Gordon has been dominating Miami's backfield work.

items.head: Will practice Friday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) will practice Friday, Barry Jackson of the Miami Herald reports. Averaging a miserable 1.9 yards per carry this season, Wright has no fantasy appeal other than being Ollie Gordon's ineffective backup.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) was limited in Thursday's practice, Marcel Louis-Jacques of ESPN.com reports. Wright has been battling various issues all season and hasn't been effective when on the field, yet he's still operating as the Dolphins' lightly-used RB2 behind Ollie Gordon. Wright is averaging a microscopic 1.9 yards per carry this season.

items.head: Returns to practice Thursday
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) is taking part in practice Thursday, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. Wright didn't practice Wednesday, so Thursday's practice appearance is a step in the right direction, but the extent of his participation remains to be seen. Ollie Gordon has cemented himself as the lead back for the Dolphins, while Wright hasn't exceeded six touches in a game this season.

items.head: Sits out first Week 9 practice
items.body: Wright (quadriceps) was a non-participant in Wednesday's practice, David Furones of the South Florida Sun Sentinel reports. In addition to a foot injury, Wright was listed with the same quad issue on the Dolphins' Week 8 injury report but proceeded to log three full practices before playing in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots. Though he played just 13 total snaps between offense and special teams in Week 8, Wright apparently emerged from the contest with his quad injury still bothering him. He'll have two more chances to get back to full practice participation prior to this Sunday's game against the Lions.

items.head: Remains non-factor in Week 8
items.body: Wright rushed two times for five yards in Sunday's 24-19 loss to the Patriots. Wright failed to catch his lone target in the passing game and remains firmly planted behind Ollie Gordon on the depth chart. While Gordon has been one of the most productive running backs on a per-carry basis this season, Wright has seemingly been stuck in the mud as a runner, averaging a pitiful 1.9 yards per carry on 22 attempts.

items.head: Titans reportedly not interested in trade
items.body: While Pollard has reportedly drawn interest from teams looking for running back help ahead of the NFL's upcoming trade deadline, Albert Breer of SI.com, Adam Schefter and Ian Rapoport note via ESPN.com that the Titans are not interested in trading him. As the trade deadline looms, there's been plenty of speculation surrounding a handful of fantasy-relevant running backs, including Pollard, who may be on the move. At this stage, he's trending toward staying put, but it's still worth keeping an antenna up on his situation through Tuesday. To date, Pollard has handled the bulk of Tennessee's carries (133), with backups Tyjae Spears and Nicholas Singleton having logged a combined 25 carries.

items.head: Set to fill backup spot
items.body: Gabriel "will serve as the backup quarterback" Sunday against the Saints, Jeremy Fowler of ESPN.com reports. It was announced earlier in the week that Shedeur Sanders would start Sunday's contest due to Deshaun Watson being in concussion protocol, and although Watson has not officially been ruled out for Week 9 as of yet, he reportedly will be. That will leave the backup spot to Gabriel, but presumably for only one contest, as the report notes Watson is expected back for Week 10.

items.head: Expected to suit up Sunday
items.body: McKee (ribs) "is expected to serve as the backup quarterback" Sunday against the Giants, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. McKee is listed as questionable for Week 9 due to what the report notes is "a cracked rib sustained on the first drive" in Week 8, but it appears he is feeling good enough to suit up. Joe Milton is set to start for the Eagles, so even if McKee is in uniform as anticipated, McKee will open the contest in a reserve role.

items.head: Pops up on injury report
items.body: McKee (rib) was limited in Thursday's practice. McKee recently lost the starting quarterback job to Joe Milton. As if things couldn't get any worse, the signal-caller appears to be in danger of missing the NFC East showdown with the Giants. If McKee can't suit up for that contest, 2026 fifth-round pick Cole Payton would presumably back up Milton against New York in Week 9.

items.head: Benched for Joe Milton in Week 9
items.body: McKee will shift to a backup role for Sunday's game against the Giants with the Eagles set to move forward with Joe Milton as their starting quarterback in Week 9, Adam Schefter of ESPN and Mike Garafolo of NFL Network report. Just two days after announcing that McKee would draw a fourth straight start this weekend, head coach Nick Sirianni appears to have changed his tune. The Eagles' decision to move forward with Milton comes after McKee went 0-3 as a starter while completing 63.2 percent of his passes for 5.6 yards per attempt and a 2:2 TD:INT since replacing Jalen Hurts (calf) atop the depth chart. Since McKee is set to become a free agent next spring and may not be part of the Eagles' long-term plans, he could end up serving as the No. 3 quarterback if the team wants to give rookie fifth-round pick Cole Payton the opportunity to suit up on game days.

items.head: Plans to return this season
items.body: Jackson, who is scheduled to undergo surgery on his injured right thumb, has told teammates he plans to return later this season, Ian Rapoport of NFL Network reports. Jackson dislocated and fractured his right thumb on his only play of last Sunday's loss at Buffalo, and while he was placed on injured reserve Thursday, he hasn't been ruled out for the season. Considering the typical recovery for his particular injury is in the 6-to-9-week range, per Rapoport, Jackson has a chance to return before the end of the regular season, but the Ravens will need to stay in the playoff hunt. To that end, Baltimore obtained Jacoby Brissett from Arizona this week to bolster a QB room that not only lost Jackson indefinitely but also Tyler Huntley for the season due to a turf-toe injury. Brissett's experience gives the team a chance to get back to winning ways after losin

items.head: Multiple factors at play in possible return
items.body: Jackson's odds to play again this season depend on his recovery from a right thumb injury, and also whether or not new QB Jacoby Brissett can keep the Ravens in the playoff picture long enough to make a return late in the season possible for Jackson, Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. The Ravens already have cycled through three starting QBs this season, and with Tyler Huntley sidelined for the rest of the campaign due to a turf-toe injury and Jackson out indefinitely, the team agreed to a trade with the Cardinals for Brissett, which became official Friday. Brissett was serviceable until he wasn't in Arizona, finishing his 2026 season there with 1,719 yards on 63 percent passing, 10 touchdowns and seven interceptions in eight appearances, and he'll have top talents in RB Derrick Henry and WR Zay Flowers to work with in his new locale. It remains to be seen if Baltimore, which is three games in the loss column behind Pittsburgh and Cincinnati in the AFC North, can get back

items.head: Officially placed on IR
items.body: The Ravens have officially placed Jackson (thumb) on injured reserve. Prior to Thursday night's game against the Jaguars, the Ravens made a trio of moves to re-shape their Week 9 QB corps. Along with Jackson, Tyler Huntley (toe) landed on IR, while Austin Reed was added to the team's active roster. As a result, Joe Fagnano (Thursday's starter), Kedon Slovis and Austin Reed are available to face Jacksonville, and then in the coming days Jacoby Brissett will be on his way to Baltimore via a looming trade with the Cardinals. Jackson will miss his team's next four games, at a minimum, and it's possible that his injury could be season ending, an outcome that is already reportedly in the cards for Huntley.

items.head: Dyami Brown (Calf) is Injured Reserve
items.body: The Commanders placed Brown (calf) on injured reserve Saturday.

items.head: Bumps up from practice squad
items.body: The Eagles elevated Mitchell from the practice squad to the active roster Saturday ahead of Sunday's game against the Giants. This marks Mitchell's third elevation of the campaign, meaning Philadelphia will need to sign him to the active roster after Week 9 if there's an expectation that he'll remain the team's No. 2 RB behind Saquon Barkley. With Barkley not operating at 100 percent last Sunday at Washington, Mitchell handled 57 percent of the snaps to the former's 32 percent, but Barkley's 14 touches went for 54 yards from scrimmage and one TD, while Mitchell produced just 37 total yards on 15 touches. The breakdown of work may skew more in Barkley's direction this week considering he entered the weekend without a designation for Sunday's matchup, but Mitchell figures to remains involved out of the Eagles backfie

items.head: Christian Kirk (Knee - Meniscus) is Injured Reserve
items.body: The 49ers placed Kirk (knee) on injured reserve Saturday.

items.head: May need meniscus surgery
items.body: Kirk (knee) will miss Sunday's game against Las Vegas and may need surgery for a meniscus injury, David Lombardi of SFStandard.com reports. After opening the year on injured reserve with a calf injury, Kirk finally got healthy and played 20 snaps in a Week 7 loss to Atlanta. Other injuries at wide receiver opened up an opportunity, but now it seems Kirk is more likely to go back on IR than make an impact in the coming weeks.

items.head: Doesn't practice Thursday
items.body: Kirk (knee) didn't practice Thursday, Sam Warren of The Athletic reports. Kirk kicked off Week 9 prep with a limited session Wednesday due to a knee injury, so his downgrade one day later may be cause for concern. Friday's practice report could provide some clarity surrounding his status ahead of Sunday's game against the Raiders.

items.head: Brian Robinson Jr. (Hamstring) is Injured Reserve
items.body: Robinson (hamstring) was placed on injured reserve Saturday, Marc Raimondi of ESPN.com reports.

items.head: Ruled out for Sunday's game
items.body: Robinson (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Bengals, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports. Though Robinson was able to practice in a limited capacity Wednesday through Friday and was initially deemed questionable for Week 9, he was downgraded shortly thereafter and will not be available for Sunday's game in Madrid. In Robinson's continued absence, look for Khalil Herbert to be elevated from the practice squad to work in a complementary role behind Bijan Robinson.

items.head: Limited at practice Thursday
items.body: Robinson (hamstring) was a limited participant in Thursday's practice, Tori McElhaney of the Falcons' official site reports. Robinson also was deemed limited on Wednesday's estimated injury report, which gives the running back one more opportunity to upgrade to full participation before the team assigns Week 9 injury designations. If he's able to return from a two-game absence Sunday against the Bengals, he'd slot back into a complementary role behind Bijan Robinson, an assignment that Khalil Herbert handled in Weeks 7 and 8.

items.head: Opens week with limited practice
items.body: The Falcons listed Robinson (hamstring) as a limited participant on Wednesday's estimated practice report, Tori McElhaney of the team's official site reports. After landing in Spain early Wednesday in advance of Sunday's game versus the Bengals in Madrid, the Falcons opted to hold a walkthrough rather than a traditional practice. Robinson was able to do enough to garner a limited listing on the injury report, marking the first time since Week 7 that he's gone down as anything other than a non-participant in practice. If Robinson can get back to full activity Thursday or Friday, he'll put himself on track to be available as the top complement to lead back Bijan Robinson on Sunday.

items.head: Won't play in Week 9
items.body: Jennings (calf) has been ruled out for Monday's contest versus the Bills. Per head coach Kevin O'Connell, Jennings suffered a calf injury at Thursday's practice that is serious enough to sideline him for at least one game. Jennings' next chance for game action is Sunday, Nov. 15 in Green Bay, while Tai Felton and Myles Price are in for some offensive snaps this week behind the top WR duo of Justin Jefferson and Jordan Addison.

items.head: DNP Friday
items.body: Jennings (calf) did not participate in Friday's practice. Jennings downgraded his practice participation Friday after being limited in Thursday's session. The wide receiver will likely need to show up in some capacity Saturday for a chance to suit up for Monday night's primetime showdown with the Bills.

items.head: Set to play in Week 9
items.body: Coleman (shoulder) doesn't have a designation for Monday's contest in Minnesota. Per Katherine Fitzgerald of The Buffalo News, Coleman again was spotted in a red non-contact jersey Saturday and eventually went down as a limited participant for a third consecutive practice. Despite the restrictions this week, though, Coleman is ready to suit up for an eighth straight game to begin the season, having put up a 20-287-3 line on 27 targets to date.

items.head: Limited at practice again
items.body: Coleman (shoulder) was a limited practice participant Friday. Coleman is on the injury report for the first time since Week 4, listed as a limited participant Thursday and Friday due to a shoulder injury. There's been no indication it's serious, so Coleman seems on track to play Monday night at Minnesota. Fellow Bills wideout DJ Moore (shoulder) also is gearing up to play.

items.head: Limited Thursday
items.body: Coleman (shoulder) was limited in practice Thursday. It's a new injury for Coleman, who is on the injury report for the first time since Week 4. With both DJ Moore (knee) and Dalton Kincaid (chest) healthy last Sunday against the Ravens, Coleman caught just one pass for four yards on three targets.

items.head: Cut loose by Saints
items.body: The Saints waived Miller on Saturday, Nick Underhill of NewOrleans.Football reports. Miller has a 20-carry outing in Week 6 at the Giants on his resume this season, but he otherwise has 46 touches in his five other appearances and overall is averaging a miserable 2.8 yards per rush. The Saints thus will be rolling with Alvin Kamara, Audric Estime and potentially practice-squad members Jarquez Hunter and Zamir White out of the backfield Sunday against the Browns. CJ Donaldson (shoulder/concussion) is sidelined.

items.head: Trade out of Baltimore unlikely
items.body: The Ravens aren't expected to deal Henry before Tuesday's trade deadline, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports. With Baltimore sitting at 4-5 and having lost its top two QBs in Lamar Jackson (thumb) and Tyler Huntley (toe) for the foreseeable future and rest of the season, respectively, there has been speculation Henry may be available via trade, but the team has informed the running back that it doesn't intend to consider such a transaction. Instead, the Ravens have dealt for quarterback Jacoby Brissett from the Cardinals to help stabilize the offense, which may help Henry end his streak being held under 100 yards rushing at four contests. Overall, Henry has racked up 689 yards and eight touchdowns on 175 carries for a career-low 3.9 YPC in his nine appearances in 2026.

items.head: Another tough night in loss
items.body: Henry rushed 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday night. He also completed one pass attempt for minus-3 yards. With Joe Fagnano under center, the Jaguars unsurprisingly had the luxury of loading up to slow down Henry, and Jacksonville already came into the contest boasting an elite run defense to begin with. Henry therefore ran into a proverbial brick wall for most of the night, and he finished under 60 rushing yards for the fourth consecutive game. However, help is on the way, as impending trade acquisition Jacoby Brissett could be ready to make his first start for the Ravens as soon as a Week 10 home matchup against the Chargers on Monday night, Nov. 16.

items.head: Dealing with Grade 2 strain
items.body: Murray (hamstring) is recovering from a Grade 2 strain "that will keep him out for Monday's game and potentially beyond," Tom Pelissero of Netflix reports. Murray has not been officially ruled out for Monday's matchup with the Bills, but Carson Wentz will start under center regardless of Murray's availability, and the latest report indicates that may not be a one-week occurrence. The Vikings will reveal whether or not Murray has any chance to suit up for Week 9 when they release their final injury report of the week later Saturday.

items.head: Likely out Monday, won't go on IR
items.body: Murray likely won't play Monday against the Bills due to a hamstring strain, Alec Lewis of The Athletic reports. Per head coach Kevin O'Connell, Murray is considered week-to-week, paving the way for Carson Wentz to make his second start of the season when the Vikings face the Bills on MNF. Per Lewis, O'Connell said Thursday that a stint on injured reserve isn't under consideration for Murray, suggesting that the starting quarterback's potential absence isn't expected to linger beyond 1-to-3 weeks.

items.head: Records one catch in Week 9 defeat
items.body: Hibner logged one reception for five yards on two targets in Thursday's loss to Baltimore. Hibner ranked second among Baltimore tight ends with 30 offensive snaps, just behind Mark Andrews (32). The former didn't do much with the opportunity, but it was a very quiet game for the Ravens' passing game as a whole, as starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Baltimore will likely have the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett starting behind center for the team's next game (Monday, Oct. 16 versus the Chargers), but Hibner has just six catches across eight contests this season, so he's not a viable fantasy option regardless of who is throwing him the ball.

items.head: Shut out in Week 9 loss
items.body: Lane did not draw a target Thursday in a loss to Jacksonville. Lane logged 32 offensive snaps, third-most among Baltimore wideouts behind Zay Flowers (37) and Rashod Bateman (35). However, Lane failed to haul in a pass (and to even see a target) for the first time this season. That can be partly attributed to quarterback play, as Ravens starting QB Joe Fagnano threw for just 60 yards. Jacoby Brissett, who Baltimore recently traded for, will likely start behind center in Week 10 against the Chargers on Monday, Nov. 16, which would improve Lane's outlook to some degree. However, he's caught one or fewer passes in three of his five games so far this season, so Lane isn't a recommended fantasy play regardless of who is starting at QB for Baltimore.

items.head: Cut by Philadelphia
items.body: The Eagles released Pierce (undisclosed) from IR with an injury settlement Friday, Dave Zangaro of NBC Sports Philadelphia reports. Pierce had been placed on injured reserve Oct. 28 due to an undisclosed issue. That was going to require him to miss at least four contests, but with the injury settlement, the veteran running back is now a free agent and is eligible to suit up as soon as he finds work with another club. Pierce appeared in three games with Philadelphia before being let go, rushing 37 times for 96 yards and two touchdowns while adding seven catches for 14 yards on 11 targets. He also took some turns as a kick returner, which could help him in his quest to latch on with another organization.

items.head: Set up for another start
items.body: Cooper and Makai Lemon are positioned to start again Sunday against the Giants, with fellow wideouts DeVonta Smith (hamstring) and Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) ruled out for a third straight game, per PhiladelphiaEagles.com. Cooper made some big plays earlier this season but hasn't done much with his more recent opportunity, catching just three of nine targets for 36 yards over the past two weeks while playing 94 percent of snaps on offense. He's been targeted on just 13 percent of his routes this year, though that rate could improve some with strong-armed Joe Milton replacing Tanner McKee as the starting QB this week.

items.head: Questionable to return from IR
items.body: Robinson (ankle) is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Raiders, with 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan saying Friday that the wideout likely will be activated from injured reserve, Nick Wagoner of ESPN.com reports. San Francisco GM John Lynch also made optimistic comments about Robinson, who was a limited practice participant Wednesday through Friday. With WRs Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring) out for at least one more week, Robinson would join Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks and Jacob Cowing as the healthy wide receivers on the active roster. The 49ers need to activate Robinson by 4  p.m. ET on Saturday to have him available for Sunday's home game against the Raiders.

items.head: Remains limited Thursday
items.body: Robinson (ankle) practiced on a limited basis Thursday. Since the 49ers designated him for return from injured reserve Wednesday, Robinson has logged back-to-back capped sessions. GM John Lynch said Thursday on KNBR radio that the 49ers expect Robinson to be available Sunday against the Raiders, which can't be said for fellow WRs Mike Evans (Achilles) and Deebo Samuel (hamstring), per Matt Maiocco of NBC Sports Bay Area. Friday's injury report will reveal Robinson's odds to return this weekend, but he'll still need to be activated by Saturday afternoon to have a chance to do so.

items.head: Good to go
items.body: Johnson (illness) was a full practice participant Friday. A quick return after Thursday's absence confirms Johnson isn't dealing with a serious illness. He should be fine for his usual role on passing downs Monday night at Minnesota.

items.head: Sick Thursday
items.body: Johnson (illness) did not practice Thursday. Johnson will have an extra day to rest up this week, as the Bills host the Vikings on Monday night. Buffalo's preferred pass-catching back, Johnson has rushed six times for just 10 yards through six games this season, but he has caught all 15 of his targets for 174 yards.

items.head: Practices fully Friday
items.body: Kincaid (chest) was a full participant in Friday's practice. Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo previously noted that Kincaid had shed his red non-contact jersey at Friday's practice, and the tight end's full participation in the session paves the way for him to be in uniform Monday night against the Vikings. Over his last two games, Kincaid (who overall is tied for first among Bills in catches (27) and leads the team in receiving yards (401)) has logged an 11-124-1 receiving line, a pace that keeps him relevant from a fantasy perspective.

items.head: Ditches non-contact jersey
items.body: Kincaid (chest) is no longer in a red non-contact jersey at Friday's practice, Sal Capaccio of WGR Sports Radio 550 Buffalo reports. With Kincaid having been listed as a limited participant Thursday while dealing with a chest injury, shedding the non-contact jersey Friday is a positive sign for his practice progression and should put the tight end in the clear for Monday night's date with a tough Vikings defense.

items.head: Limited at practice Thursday
items.body: Kincaid (chest) was listed as a limited participant in Thursday's practice,. Fellow pass catchers DJ Moore (shoulder) and Keon Coleman (shoulder) also were limited Thursday, so the trio's statuses will need to be monitored ahead of Monday night's game against the Vikings. Over his last two outings, Kincaid has managed to make his mark from a fantasy perspective by logging an 11-124-1 receiving line in that span.

items.head: Won't play Sunday
items.body: Shaheed (knee) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, Gregg Bell of 933 KJR reports. With Shaheed out last week, Tory Horton handled a 72 percent route share in Seattle's loss to Chicago. It'll likely be a similar look this week with Horton and Cooper Kupp taking most of the WR snaps alongside Jaxon Smith-Njigba. The big difference will be under center, where Drew Lock is filling in for Sam Darnold (quad) for the second time this season.

items.head: Misses another practice
items.body: Shaheed (knee) didn't participate at the Seahawks' practice Thursday, John Boyle of the team's official site reports. Shaheed has now missed back-to-back practices to open the week as he continues to work his way back from the knee injury that forced him to miss the team's Week 8 loss to Chicago. The wide receiver's chances to play Sunday versus Arizona seem thin, so Tory Horton could serve as the team's No. 3 option at wide receiver again in Week 9.

items.head: DNP on Wednesday
items.body: Shaheed (knee) did not practice Wednesday, John Boyle of the Seahawks' official site reports. Shaheed missed Monday night's loss to the Bears, which allowed Tory Horton to log a season-high 43 offensive snaps, which he turned into a 3-26-0 receiving line on six targets. Horton would again be in line for WR3 duties if Shaheed needs to sit Sunday against Arizona.

items.head: Iffy for Week 9
items.body: Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said Tuesday that Shaheed (knee) has a chance to play Sunday against the Cardinals, Brady Henderson of ESPN.com reports. Shaheed was sidelined for the first time all season in Monday's 34-17 loss to the Bears, after his knee injury kept him from practicing throughout the week. In Shaheed's absence, Tory Horton handled elevated snaps as the Seahawks' No. 3 wideout behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Cooper Kupp, while George Holani served as the team's top kickoff returner. Shaheed may need to turn in a full practice at some point during Week 9 prep to put himself on track to return to action Sunday.

items.head: Won't play Sunday
items.body: Smith (hamstring) has been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Giants. Smith thus will sit out for the fifth time in six games due to a hamstring injury. Fellow WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) also won't play Sunday, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore to man the Eagles' receiving corps. Smith's next chance to suit up is Sunday, Nov. 22, versus the Steelers.

items.head: Not present at Friday's practice
items.body: Smith (hamstring) was not seen at Friday's practice, Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer reports. With Smith now absent from practice again Friday, he's unlikely to play Sunday against the Giants, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper and Hollywood Brown as the top wide receivers for QB Joe Milton's first start in an Eagles uniform. Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) was also absent from practice Friday and figures to join Smith on the gameday inactive list yet again.

items.head: Non-participant again Thursday
items.body: Smith (hamstring) wasn't spotted at practice Thursday, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports. Smith hasn't practiced or played since he suited up for Philadelphia's Week 6 loss to the Panthers. He's trending toward a third consecutive absence Sunday against the Giants. With Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) also yet to resume practicing, Makai Lemon looks set to lead Philadelphia's receiving corps for a third consecutive game.

items.head: Not present Wednesday
items.body: Smith (hamstring) wasn't spotted at Wednesday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports. Smith has missed four of the last five contests due to a lingering hamstring injury, and until he's able to mix into drills again, he may not be a candidate to be active on game days. The Eagles have a Week 10 bye after Sunday's matchup with the Giants, so the team could be focusing on getting him healthy for Week 11 and beyond. In any case, fellow WR Dontayvion Wicks (ankle) also wasn't seen Wednesday, leaving Makai Lemon, Darius Cooper, Hollywood Brown and Elijah Moore as the healthy options at the position on the active roster.

items.head: Ruled out for Sunday's game
items.body: Wicks (ankle) is listed as out for Sunday's game against the Giants. After sitting out practice Friday, Wicks will miss a third straight game for Philadelphia. He'll now have the team's Week 10 bye to try and get right coming out of the break. The Eagles will continue to roll with Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper as their Nos. 1 and 2 receivers against New York this week.

items.head: Still sidelined Friday
items.body: Wicks (ankle) is not practicing Friday, Andrew DiCecco of InsideTheBirds.com reports. Wicks hasn't practiced at all this week and looks extremely unlikely to play Sunday against the Giants. With DeVonta Smith (hamstring) also injured, the Eagles likely will keep rolling with Makai Lemon and Darius Cooper as their every-down wideouts.

items.head: Not spotted again Thursday
items.body: Wicks (ankle) wasn't present for Thursday's practice, Brooks Kubena of The Athletic reports. Wicks continues to sit out drills for a third straight week due to an ankle injury.
